analysis:
The failure has a precise mechanism, stated in synthesis §1. Pointwise RMSE/MAE is dominated by each gene's baseline fitness level (the "gene-mean"). A regression model can score decent RMSE by fitting (a) gene means and (b) the population condition effect — which conditions hurt MOST genes — while learning NOTHING about the gene x condition interaction, which is the actual biological signal ("which conditions stress THIS gene"). The project later confirmed the population effect is worthless for ranking: the chem-NULL baseline (population condition profile, gene-identity-free) scores ~0 within-gene Spearman. So optimizing MSE/MAE across ~54k rows optimizes the wrong quantity for the ranking objective.

Two reasons are specific to the cross-ORGANISM setting: (1) Homology distance (S1 diagnostic, H-HOMO-01 at 1.6 sigma): a held-out organism's genes lie far from any training gene in ProteomeLM embedding space, so the model has no nearby anchor to place them. (2) Fitness-blindness of the embedding: ProteomeLM encodes sequence/structure/proteome-context, not how a gene responds to stressors; cross-org compounds this with distribution shift. Evidence for (2): ProteomeLM beat raw ESM-C by only ~0.006 RMSE (T5-C), so even the proteome-contextual machinery added almost no conditional signal.

The T1/T4/T5 ledger entries corroborate the "RMSE was fine but sub-threshold and metric-conflicted" picture: across the entire T1-T5 sweep every arm sat at RMSE ~0.50-0.52 with sub-threshold gaps, MSE and Huber conflicted on RMSE vs MAE, and only one intervention (T5-A adapter dim-reduction) produced any statistically robust gain — and it was still 20% of the RMSE threshold. None of this moved the within-gene ranking, which is why the project pivoted to the R-regime (within-organism, ranking metric).
caveats: The 0.045 Spearman and the ~0.43 replicate noise floor are quoted from the SCIENTIFIC_SYNTHESIS narrative (§1), not from a committed metrics artifact reproduced in this dashboard pass — hence verification=ledger. Later synthesis (§3) reports a slightly different replicate ceiling (Spearman ~0.39 / NDCG@5 ~0.66) for the WITHIN-organism task; §1's ~0.43 is the cross-organism-context noise floor. The ~0.045 is described as "statistically indistinguishable from random," not a precisely CI-bounded estimate. The T1/T4/T5 ledger RMSE/MAE tables use the multi_org_balanced split and report co-primary RMSE/MAE only; the within-gene Spearman for the cross-org regime is carried in the synthesis, not tabulated per-arm in those three decision files. NDCG@5 was NOT a T-regime metric — the T-regime pre-dates the R-regime metric change (RMSE -> per-gene ranking), so no NDCG@5 number exists for cross-org. The gate values referenced for reader orientation (chem-kNN NDCG@5 0.485, replicate ceiling 0.66) belong to the later within-organism R-regime, not to this T-regime experiment.
how_tested:
DATA. Tn-seq gene-fitness measurements across a large multi-organism bacterial/archaeal panel (48 organisms were re-encoded in T5; the training split drew from the full org pool). Each row is one (gene, experimental condition) pair with a continuous fitness score. Inputs per row: a frozen ProteomeLM-L layer-8 gene embedding (1152-dim, mean-pooled, sequence-derived, proteome-contextualized, never fine-tuned) concatenated with a media-chemistry encoding of the condition.

SPLIT (the key design). Cross-ORGANISM holdout, i.e. leave-genomes-out: the canonical split protocol was `multi_org_balanced` (locked in `data_contract/splits/locked_protocol.yaml`). Whole organisms were held out for validation so that held-out orgs are NOT in train (leakage/split-overlap guardrails explicitly passed "by construction" in T1-DEC-001). The reported per-organism validation set covered 4 val organisms (ANA3, BFirm, pseudo3_N2E3, SyringaeB728a_mexBdelta in the T1 breakdown). All preprocessing (chemistry vocab, scalers, eligibility thresholds) was fit on train rows only; unseen val categories mapped to explicit <UNK>. Feature contract frozen at artifact de21504134c84a6c.

OBJECTIVE / WHAT WAS RUN. Pointwise regression on the raw continuous fitness score. The pre-registered co-primary metrics were RMSE and MAE (S2-locked thresholds RMSE=0.0212, MAE=0.005). The loss was mean squared error (MSE); T4-A explicitly tested Huber (delta 0.5/1.0/1.5) vs MSE and T4-B tested per-experiment z-scored targets vs raw — MSE + raw targets were retained. Model families swept across tiers: a shallow concat-linear MLP (T1, hidden 256), a 2-layer ResidualMLP (hidden 512, T3), plus encoder/layer/embedding ablations (T5). Training config throughout: 3 seeds {0,1,2}, 8 epochs, constant lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4, batch_size=8192; cross-seed std reported; seed-0 bootstrap CIs (1000 row-resamples).

BASELINES / CONTROLS in the T-regime. The learned models were required to beat the locked S2 best-non-global baseline (embedding-NN, RMSE 0.5884 on multi_org_balanced) — which they did by ~0.07 RMSE. Ablation controls established the embedding was not the fixable lever: T5-B (PLM layer 0/4/8/12/18) and T5-C (ProteomeLM layer-8 vs raw ESM-C 600M) — ProteomeLM beat raw ESM-C by only ~0.006 RMSE.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT MATTERED. Beyond the co-primary RMSE/MAE, the project computed the biologically meaningful quantity: the within-GENE ranking of a gene's conditions (within-gene Spearman), compared against a replicate noise floor (~0.43 Spearman, the agreement between biological replicates = achievable ceiling). This is what exposed the failure. A supporting mechanism-check (run later, in the R-regime) confirmed the population/cross-gene condition profile carries essentially no within-gene signal: the chem-NULL baseline (predict the population condition profile, no gene specificity) scores ~0 within-gene Spearman. The homology cause was quantified in S1 (H-HOMO-01, 1.6 sigma: held-out-org genes far from any train gene in embedding space), and T1 reported a homology-bin RMSE breakdown (val rows binned by cosine to nearest train gene) confirming error grows with homology distance (RMSE ~0.40 at cosine <0.5 rising to ~0.55 at cosine >0.85).
hypothesis: Foundational bet: a frozen, proteome-contextualized, sequence-derived protein embedding (ProteomeLM) combined with a media-chemistry encoding contains enough information to predict conditional gene essentiality, and this generalizes across organisms. Concretely for this experiment: train pointwise MSE/MAE regression on fitness for a pool of organisms, hold entire genomes out, and predict held-out organisms' gene x condition fitness — expecting both good error metrics AND a biologically meaningful within-gene ordering of conditions.
meaning: This is the pivotal negative that reframed the entire project. It cleanly separated two problems that RMSE conflates: predicting the LEVEL of fitness (easy, gene-mean-dominated, achieved) versus predicting the within-gene conditional ORDERING (the real, hard, biologically useful problem). Cross-organism transfer of the ordering is ~0 — frozen protein embeddings carry no transferable conditional-response information across genomes, for two reasons (homology distance + a fitness-blind embedding). The consequences: (1) the generalization claim was narrowed from cross-organism to WITHIN-organism (predict a known organism's genes under novel condition combinations); (2) the primary metric was changed from RMSE to per-gene ranking (within-gene Spearman + NDCG@k), the quantity a biologist actually uses. Everything in the later R-regime — the chem-kNN strong baseline, the memorization-dominated finding, the cold-gene diagnostic — descends from this result. It also set the durable lesson that a low RMSE can entirely hide a useless model when the target is heavy-tailed and gene-mean-dominated.
name: Cross-organism fitness regression (T-regime)

results.label: Within-gene Spearman (cross-organism holdout, the diagnostic that mattered)
results.plain_explanation: This is the headline failure. Spearman rank correlation runs -1 to +1; 0 means the model's ordering of a gene's conditions is no better than random, +1 is perfect. At ~0.045 the model has essentially NO ability to say which conditions stress a given gene most — it is statistically indistinguishable from random guessing. Bad, and it is the biologically meaningful quantity (a biologist wants the ranking, not the raw score). Crucially, RMSE/MAE looked fine at the same time, which is exactly the trap: good error metrics hid a useless ranking.

results.label: Replicate noise floor / achievable ceiling (within-gene Spearman, cross-org context)
results.plain_explanation: The ceiling of what is even achievable: two biological replicates of the SAME experiment only agree at ~0.43 within-gene Spearman, because the target is intrinsically noisy. So the honest scale runs 0 (random) to ~0.43 (as good as a repeat of the experiment). The model landed at ~0.045 — near the floor, nowhere near the ceiling. This reframes the ~0.045 as unambiguously a failure, not a hard-target artifact: a repeat experiment does ~10x better.

results.label: Model RMSE on multi_org_balanced (representative locked model, T4/T5 sweep)
results.plain_explanation: RMSE is prediction error on the raw fitness score (lower is better, same units as fitness). Around 0.50 it was 'acceptable' and beat the locked non-global baseline (embedding-NN at 0.5884) by ~0.07. This is the 'fine' half of the story — the error metric the model was TRAINED on looked healthy. The problem is RMSE is dominated by each gene's baseline fitness level (the gene-mean), so a low RMSE is achievable while the gene x condition interaction — the actual signal — is learned not at all.

results.label: MAE on multi_org_balanced (representative locked model)
results.plain_explanation: Mean absolute error on raw fitness, lower is better. ~0.28 was likewise 'fine' and stable across seeds. Together with RMSE ~0.50 it completes the picture: both pointwise error co-primaries were satisfactory, yet the within-gene ranking was random — the two are measuring different things.

results.label: ProteomeLM layer-8 vs raw ESM-C 600M advantage (T5-C, evidence for the fitness-blind cause)
results.plain_explanation: This tiny gap is the evidence for cause #2. Swapping the full proteome-contextual ProteomeLM embedding for a raw per-protein ESM-C embedding barely changed error (~0.006 RMSE, ~28% of the promotion threshold). Interpretation: even the sophisticated proteome-context machinery added almost no CONDITIONAL signal — the embedding encodes sequence/structure, not how a gene responds to stressors. A near-zero contribution from the 'smart' part of the embedding is consistent with the ranking being random.

results.label: Best T-regime intervention gain (T5-A adapter_1024_proj, dimension-reduction adapter)
results.number: RMSE -0.0043, MAE -0.0025 (0.4991 vs 0.5034; disjoint bootstrap CIs)
results.plain_explanation: The single statistically robust improvement found in the entire T2-T5 architecture sweep — and it was still only ~20% of the RMSE promotion threshold and ~50% of the MAE threshold. A directional win, not a paradigm shift. It illustrates that no amount of encoder/architecture tuning within the frozen-embedding + pointwise-regression + cross-org frame moved the needle on the real problem; the ranking stayed ~random regardless.

results.label: Homology cause strength (S1 diagnostic, H-HOMO-01)
results.plain_explanation: Quantifies cause #1 (homology distance). Held-out organisms' genes sit far from any training gene in embedding space, a ~1.6-sigma effect, so the model has no nearby anchor to place them. T1's homology-bin RMSE breakdown corroborates it: error rises monotonically with cosine distance to the nearest train gene (RMSE ~0.40 for the closest bin, cosine <0.5, up to ~0.55 for the farthest, cosine >0.85). This is why cross-ORGANISM specifically fails harder than the later cross-GENE-within-organism (cold-gene) regime, where the embedding does generalize.

name: The within-organism test harness (split · eligibility · metric · baselines · gate)
hypothesis: A single locked within-organism test harness — a cold-condition holdout split, a spread-based eligibility filter, a retrieval-first metric with hierarchical confidence intervals, three matched baselines, and a replicate ceiling — is a valid and sufficient lens to judge whether ANY learned model earns promotion for the "find a gene's top stressor conditions" task. Concretely: hold out 20% of each organism's conditions (which are chemically disjoint from train, so the task is genuine composition not recall); score only genes that vary enough to be rankable (tail_g over a per-org noise-scaled threshold); score the model and every baseline on the identical eligible val genes; and promote only if the model beats the chem-kNN gate by an effect-size margin with disjoint org→gene bootstrap CIs.
how_tested: This is the shared test harness every within-organism ranking experiment runs through, defined across four locked decisions (R-LOCK-1 through R-LOCK-4, 2026-05-24 to 2026-05-25) and implemented in src/ranking/eval/harness.py. WHAT DATA: Tn-seq fitness values ("fit") for genes across growth conditions, per organism; a condition is keyed as condition_key = (expDesc, media, temperature). Population characterization spanned 48 organisms, 182,447 (org, gene) pairs, ~7,500 experiment assays, ~4,200 distinct conditions; the reliable-replicate headline subset is 23 orgs. THE SPLIT (R-LOCK-2): within each organism, hold out 20% of the DISTINCT conditions (fraction-based because org sizes span 17x), seed 0, with floor 3 / cap 30 held-out conditions per org. Holdout is at the CONDITION level, not the assay (expName) level — every replicate assay of a held-out condition goes to val together (hold_out_together) so no replicate of a val condition leaks into train. Held out at the condition level, val conditions turn out to be 100% chemically disjoint from train ("cold columns"; verified 0/78 overlap), so the model must COMPOSE gene embedding x condition chemistry rather than recall the exact condition — this is the deployment-relevant "novel conditions within a known organism" claim. Splits are stratified by expGroup where feasible; seeds 0/1/2 for multi-seed checks; Keio is the dev subset. THE ELIGIBILITY FILTER (R-LOCK-1): only rank genes that actually vary across conditions. Spread is measured as tail_g = p95 - p5 of a gene's fit across its conditions (NOT IQR — a gene essential in only 3-5 of 100 conditions has IQR ~ 0 yet is the single most rankable gene, so IQR would discard exactly the best targets). A gene is eligible if tail_g exceeds a PER-ORG threshold tail_min_org = max(0.20, 0.80 x (1 - r_replicate_org)), where r_replicate_org is that org's replicate reproducibility — noisier orgs (which span 5.4x, replicate Spearman 0.16 to 0.89) demand a higher spread bar. Val is HARD-filtered on this (m_min_val = 5 conditions; Spearman is undefined on constant fit). Train genes are all kept but WEIGHTED by w_g = clip((tail_g - tail_min_org)/(p75_org - tail_min_org),0,1) x min(m_g/m_min,1), so low-spread genes contribute little but still anchor the "predict near-flat for non-conditional genes" variance prior. DENOMINATOR PARITY: the model and every baseline are scored on the IDENTICAL eligible val gene set (min 5 conditions/gene, non-constant). THE THREE BASELINES (all in harness.py, split-specific for the cold-column primary split): (1) chem-NULL = chemistry_nearest_condition_profile — for a held-out condition c, find its chemically-nearest TRAIN condition c' by cosine distance on condition features and predict every gene's fit at c as the train-gene MEAN fit at c'; gene-blind population profile, the floor a real model must clear. (2) chem-kNN = chemistry_knn_predict (k=5) — predict gene g's fit at cold condition c from g's OWN train fit at its k chemically-nearest train conditions; it uses the gene's warm history bridged by chemistry and is the competitive gate. (3) linear inductive-MF = inductive_mf_predict — a bilinear model Fit[g,c] = U[g]·(W·x[c]) + b[g] with free per-gene latents U (genes are warm), a chemistry-feature column map W·x[c] that places COLD conditions via their features, and per-gene bias b, trained by (w_g-weighted) MSE; isolates whether the deep model's nonlinearity beats a linear feature-MF. THE REPLICATE NOISE FLOOR / ORACLE (R-LOCK-4, retrieval_noise_floor in harness): for each gene with >=2 replicate assays at >=5 conditions, use replicate A's fit as the PREDICTION and replicate B's fit as the TRUTH and compute NDCG@k/precision@k — the best any model could do given biological noise; reported as a ceiling line (only for the 23 orgs with adequate replicate design). METRICS (R-LOCK-4 v2): PRIMARY is NDCG@5 (retrieval; relevance = max(0,-fit) so a stronger stressor = more negative fit = higher gain, ranking conditions by predicted-most-essential first); SECONDARY/anti-gaming is within-gene Spearman and Kendall (full-list completeness). Every metric carries a HIERARCHICAL bootstrap CI: resample organisms with replacement, then genes within each chosen org (n=1000, 95% percentile) — because genes within an org are correlated, a flat bootstrap would be overconfident. THE GATE: a learned model is promoted over chem-kNN only if it beats chem-kNN by the effect-size margin (CLAUDE.md: >= ~0.026 NDCG@5) AND the two hierarchical-bootstrap CIs are DISJOINT; the harness also provides a one-sided hierarchical bootstrap p-value on the per-gene paired delta and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across a tier's arms. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN through this harness: the locked pointwise_huber model vs all three baselines, on both a fast 3-org gate (Keio+Caulo+MR1, seed 0, N=9,152 eligible val genes) and the 23-org / 3-seed headline (N=39,356 eligible val genes), pinned in the committed artifact data_contract/ranking/reval_baseline.json.

results.label: chem-kNN gate — NDCG@5 (23-org / 3-seed headline)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 ranges 0 to 1 (higher = better top-of-list ranking). This is the value of the competitive baseline (chem-kNN: predict a gene's fit at a cold condition from that gene's OWN fit at its chemically-nearest train conditions). It is the bar any learned model must clear to be promoted. It is high because retrieving a gene's own warm history is a very strong strategy on a split that is transductive over genes.

results.label: locked model (pointwise_huber) — NDCG@5 (23-org / 3-seed)
results.plain_explanation: The best learned model's headline NDCG@5. It sits BELOW the chem-kNN gate of 0.4852 (a gap of about -0.053), so the model does NOT earn promotion on the warm within-org split. This is the honest, correctly-measured central finding the harness exists to surface: parametric learning loses to local memorization here — not because the embedding is worthless, but because looking up a gene's own past behavior is hard to beat.

results.label: linear inductive-MF — NDCG@5 (23-org / 3-seed)
results.plain_explanation: The bilinear control baseline (free per-gene latents + chemistry column factors). It lands essentially at the deep model's level (0.4290 vs 0.4319) and below chem-kNN, showing the deep model's nonlinearity buys nothing over a linear feature-MF on this task — a key negative that only a matched baseline can reveal.

results.label: chem-NULL floor — NDCG@5 (23-org / 3-seed)
results.plain_explanation: The gene-blind population baseline (nearest-chemistry train-condition mean, ignoring gene identity). It is the FLOOR: a real model must beat it. The learned model (0.4319) clears it comfortably, confirming the model captures gene-specific structure beyond the population profile even though it fails to beat the stronger chem-kNN gate.

results.label: promotion margin required over chem-kNN (NDCG@5)
results.plain_explanation: The effect-size-anchored margin (from CLAUDE.md) by which a model must beat the chem-kNN gate to be promoted, AND the two hierarchical org->gene bootstrap CIs must be disjoint. It is a deliberately strict, non-overlapping-evidence bar; the current model falls short (it is below the gate, not 0.026 above it).

results.label: hierarchical bootstrap settings
results.number: n=1000, 95% percentile, resample orgs then genes
results.plain_explanation: Every reported NDCG@5 / Spearman carries a two-level (org -> gene) bootstrap CI. Resampling organisms first, then genes within, honors that genes in one organism are correlated; a flat gene-level bootstrap would give a too-narrow (overconfident) CI and inflate false promotions. This is what makes the 'disjoint CIs' gate trustworthy.

results.label: eligible val genes scored (headline / fast gate)
results.plain_explanation: Sample sizes N for the denominator-parity comparison: the model and all three baselines are scored on exactly these same eligible val genes (genes with >=5 conditions and non-constant fit). Large N makes the bootstrap CIs tight, which is why even a ~0.05 model-vs-gate gap is a meaningful, not noise-driven, shortfall.

results.label: holdout fraction / seed / condition unit
results.plain_explanation: The split rule (R-LOCK-2): hold out 20% of each org's distinct conditions at the condition (not assay) level so replicates of a val condition never leak into train. Fraction-based (not fixed-k) because org sizes span 17x. This is what makes val columns chemically cold and the task genuine composition.

results.label: eligibility spread metric / per-org threshold
results.number: tail_g = p95 - p5; tail_min_org = max(0.20, 0.80 x (1 - r_replicate_org))
results.plain_explanation: The eligibility rule (R-LOCK-1): rank a gene only if its fit range (p95-p5) exceeds a per-org bar scaled to that org's replicate noise. tail (not IQR) is used because a gene essential in only 3-5 of 100 conditions has IQR ~ 0 but is the MOST rankable gene — IQR would throw away exactly the best targets. Noisier orgs (replicate reproducibility spans 5.4x, 0.16 to 0.89) get a higher bar.

analysis: The harness works because it forces an apples-to-apples comparison on a deliberately hard task. The split makes val conditions 100% chemically-disjoint from train ("cold columns"): the model never sees the held-out condition during training, so it can only score well by composing the gene embedding with the condition's chemistry — the deployment-relevant claim ("novel condition combinations within a known organism"). The eligibility filter (tail_g = p95 - p5 of a gene's fit across conditions, over a per-org threshold scaled to that org's replicate noise) removes flat, non-conditional genes whose ranking is meaningless/undefined, and it uses tail rather than IQR specifically because a gene essential in only 3-5 of 100 conditions has IQR ~ 0 by construction yet is exactly the most rankable target. Denominator parity — model and every baseline scored on the identical eligible val genes — is what makes the deltas trustworthy. The three baselines triangulate what "learning" would even mean: chem-NULL (gene-blind population profile via nearest-chemistry train-condition mean) is the floor a real model must clear; chem-kNN (the gene's OWN warm history retrieved through chemistry) is the hard, non-parametric bar that turns out to WIN — because the split is transductive over genes, so simply looking up a gene's past behavior beats parametric generalization; linear inductive-MF (free per-gene latents + a chemistry-feature column map, Fit[g,c]=U[g]·(W·x[c])+b[g]) is the bilinear control that isolates whether the deep model's nonlinearity buys anything. The replicate oracle (replicate A predicting replicate B) sets the attainable ceiling. The gate (beat chem-kNN by the effect-size-anchored margin with disjoint hierarchical org->gene bootstrap CIs) is deliberately strict: the hierarchical bootstrap widens the CI to respect that genes within an org are correlated, preventing overconfident "disjoint CI" promotions. CAVEATS: two versions of the metric contract exist — the original R-LOCK-4-DEC-001 (2026-05-24) locked within-gene Spearman as primary with a "per-condition train mean" baseline and flat gene-level bootstrap; the amended r_lock_4_v2 (R-LOCK-4-DEC-002, 2026-05-25, materialized in metric_contract.yaml and implemented in harness.py) supersedes it after the publication-readiness audit — NDCG@5 became primary, the hierarchical org->gene bootstrap replaced flat, and baselines became split-specific; the dashboard should describe the CURRENT (v2) harness that harness.py implements. The "~0.026 NDCG@5 margin" is the CLAUDE.md statement of the gate; metric_contract.yaml states numeric promotion deltas in Spearman/Kendall terms (0.01/0.008 absolute) plus "CIs must be disjoint" — disjoint CIs is the operative rule. The eligibility policy's per-org r_replicate values were flagged (R-LOCK-1 audit 2026-05-25) as computed on the full dataset rather than train-only — a real but small-magnitude locked-artifact violation. Threshold constants (floor 0.20, coef 0.80, tail_ref=per-org p75, holdout frac 0.20) are documented judgment calls, not derived optima. The replicate ceiling (~0.66 NDCG@5 per the brief) comes from retrieval_noise_floor and is only available for the 23 orgs with an adequate replicate design.
meaning: This harness is the measuring instrument for the entire within-organism program — every R-tier experiment (R1 chemistry, R-LOSS loss family, R-CONF, R-AUG, R-COLD, R-EVAL) inherits its split, eligibility, parity rule, baselines, and gate, so its correctness is load-bearing for all downstream verdicts. Two design choices proved decisive. First, holding out conditions (not assays) at the condition level made the val columns chemically cold, which reframed the task from easy matrix completion to genuine cold-start composition — and revealed that chem-kNN (retrieving a gene's own warm history) is a very strong, hard-to-beat bar precisely because the split is transductive over genes. That is why the headline result across the project is that the learned model does NOT beat chem-kNN on the warm within-org split (model NDCG@5 0.4319 vs gate 0.4852), which the harness reports honestly rather than hiding. Second, making NDCG@5 primary with an HONEST hierarchical bootstrap exposed that apparent wins can be CI-overlapping even when a flat bootstrap would have called them significant — the harness is what keeps the project from over-claiming promotions. In short, this infrastructure is what lets the project distinguish "the embedding is useless" (false) from "local memorization beats global parametric learning on the warm split" (the actual, correctly-measured finding).
caveats: Two versions of the metric contract exist: R-LOCK-4-DEC-001 (v1, 2026-05-24) locked within-gene Spearman as primary with a per-condition-train-mean baseline and flat gene bootstrap; r_lock_4_v2 (R-LOCK-4-DEC-002, 2026-05-25, in metric_contract.yaml + harness.py) supersedes it — NDCG@5 primary, hierarchical org->gene bootstrap, split-specific baselines. Describe the v2 harness (what harness.py implements). The ~0.026 NDCG@5 gate margin is from CLAUDE.md; the yaml states promotion deltas as Spearman 0.01 / Kendall 0.008 absolute plus mandatory disjoint CIs — disjoint CIs is the operative rule. R-LOCK-1 audit (2026-05-25) flagged that per-org r_replicate values were computed on the full dataset, not train-only — a real but small locked-artifact violation. Threshold constants (tail floor 0.20, noise coef 0.80, tail_ref = per-org p75, holdout frac 0.20) are documented judgment calls, not derived optima. Replicate ceiling (~0.66 NDCG@5) is only available for the 23 orgs with adequate replicate design. Baseline numbers are reproduced in the committed reval_baseline.json (code-verified); the split/eligibility/gate definitions are from the decision ledger + harness source (ledger-verified) — hence verification=mixed.

name: Chemistry encoder sweep (R1)
hypothesis: H-R-CHEM-01: under within-organism condition-holdout ranking ("find the top stressors for each gene"), structural chemistry fingerprints (Morgan / RDKit / MACCS) should outperform the 425-dimensional multihot chemistry baseline — reversing the earlier T6-A result, which was measured under a different (MSE + cross-organism regression) setup. Secondary prediction: any chemistry arm using the locked T5-A deep architecture should beat the non-parametric gene-specific chemistry-kNN baseline.
how_tested: Data and task: within-organism conditional-essentiality ranking on Tn-seq fitness data — for each gene the model ranks held-out experimental conditions by fitness effect. Evaluated on the 23 replicate organisms with a reliable noise floor (ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya). All arms and all baselines were scored on one common eligible validation gene set of ~46,000 genes (denominator parity). Split: a single within-organism condition-holdout split (R-LOCK-2, seed 0) — genes are seen in training, but the specific held-out conditions are not (transductive over genes). Arms: 6 chemistry-encoder arms, all on the locked T5-A deep architecture (AdapterResidualMLP over frozen ProteomeLM gene embeddings plus a chemistry-feature vector): (1) multihot_425, a 425-dim binary compound presence/absence vector (control + T-regime lock); (2) morgan_2048, 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint; (3) rdkit_2048, 2048-bit RDKit fingerprint; (4) maccs_167, 167-bit MACCS keys; (5) morgan_plus_multihot; (6) maccs_plus_multihot (the two hybrids concatenate a fingerprint with multihot). Design: 6 arms x 3 seeds (0,1,2) x 23 orgs; the 3 seeds vary only model initialization (split fixed at seed 0), so per-arm metrics are mean ± std over 3 seeds. Held-constant controls: R-LOCK-1 eligibility (tail_g / w_g weighting), R-LOCK-2 split, R-LOCK-3 pointwise sampler, R-LOCK-4 metric contract, T5-A architecture, weighted pointwise MSE loss, 8 epochs, Spearman early stopping. Baselines on the identical gene set: chem-kNN (gene-specific chemistry-similarity lookup, the bar), chem-NULL (gene-identity-free population profile, the floor), and a replicate-based noise-floor ceiling. Pre-registered promotion rule: Δ within-gene Spearman ≥ 0.023 vs chem-kNN AND beat chem-kNN on NDCG@5, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 6 arms, and must also clear the chem-NULL gate. Reported metrics: within-gene Spearman, NDCG@1, NDCG@5 (retrieval), precision@5. Artifacts referenced by the ledger: artifacts/runs/r1/r1_results.csv and r1_metric_comparison.csv.

results.label: multihot_425 NDCG@5 (best arm)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures how well the top-5 ranked conditions match the true top stressors for each gene; it ranges 0 to 1, higher is better. The multihot presence/absence encoder was the single best of the 6 arms at 0.422. This is well BELOW the chem-kNN gate of 0.485 that a learned model must beat, so even the best encoder is a clear loss. The tiny ±0.001 std across 3 seeds means the result is highly stable, not noise.

results.label: multihot_425 within-gene Spearman
results.plain_explanation: Spearman is the secondary, full-list rank-agreement metric (higher is better). The best arm reached only 0.130, far below chem-kNN's 0.240 — another decisive loss on the secondary metric, and nowhere near the +0.023 improvement the promotion rule required (it was worse, not better).

results.label: morgan_2048 NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The 2048-bit Morgan structural fingerprint scored slightly WORSE than multihot (0.415 vs 0.422). Since the hypothesis predicted fingerprints would beat multihot, this is evidence against it: structural priors did not help.

results.label: rdkit_2048 NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The RDKit fingerprint was the WEAKEST arm at 0.406 — the largest shortfall from multihot among the structural encoders, and furthest below the 0.485 chem-kNN gate. Structural information actively hurt here relative to simple presence/absence bits.

results.label: maccs_167 NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The 167-bit MACCS structural keys scored 0.414, again below multihot's 0.422. Consistent with all fingerprint arms being no-better-or-worse than the multihot control.

results.label: morgan_plus_multihot NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Concatenating Morgan with multihot gave 0.420 — essentially tied with plain multihot (0.422) and still below the 0.485 gate. Adding structural bits on top of multihot bought nothing.

results.label: maccs_plus_multihot NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The MACCS+multihot hybrid scored 0.419, again indistinguishable from plain multihot and below the gate. All 6 encoders cluster tightly around NDCG@5 ≈ 0.41–0.42.

results.label: chem-kNN gate (baseline to beat) NDCG@5 / Spearman
results.plain_explanation: chem-kNN is the non-parametric gene-specific chemistry-similarity lookup that every learned model must beat. Its NDCG@5 of 0.485 and Spearman of 0.240 sit far above the best deep-model arm (0.422 / 0.130). The gap is large and consistent across all 3 seeds (arm std ≤ 0.01), and it points in the WRONG direction — no arm is even a promotion candidate.

results.label: chem-NULL floor NDCG@5 / Spearman
results.plain_explanation: chem-NULL is the gene-identity-free floor (population-average condition profile). The deep model (0.422 NDCG@5) clearly beats this floor, showing the model has SOME real signal — but the simple gene-specific kNN lookup (0.485) is decisively better than the deep model, so the model's signal is not enough to be useful over the lookup.

results.label: noise-floor ceiling NDCG@5 / Spearman
results.plain_explanation: The replicate-based noise ceiling (~0.658 NDCG@5) is the practical upper bound set by measurement reproducibility. It frames the scale: chem-kNN at 0.485 is well along toward the ceiling, while all model arms (~0.42) lag both the ceiling and the kNN gate.

analysis: The sweep isolated the chemistry encoder while holding architecture (T5-A) and loss (pointwise MSE) fixed. Two clean findings emerged. First, structural fingerprints did NOT beat multihot — multihot_425 was the single best arm (NDCG@5 0.422), and every fingerprint arm was uniformly slightly worse (Morgan 0.415, RDKit 0.406, MACCS 0.414, hybrids ~0.42), so H-R-CHEM-01 was rejected in the same direction as the earlier T6-A result. The likely mechanism: dataset S1 has ≥95% chemistry overlap between train and held-out conditions, so held-out conditions are recombinations of already-seen chemicals; multihot's exact-match bits are already lossless in that regime, leaving little novel chemistry for a fingerprint's structural smoothness to generalize over. Second and more decisive, NO arm beat the chem-kNN gate — the best model (0.422 / 0.130) lost to chem-kNN (0.485 / 0.240) by a wide, seed-consistent margin (std ≤ 0.01), far larger than the 0.023 promotion delta and in the wrong direction, so FDR correction was moot. The model does beat the chem-NULL floor (0.422 vs 0.343), so it has some signal, but the interpretation is architectural/objective rather than representational: the locked deep model under pointwise MSE cannot beat a non-parametric gene-specific similarity lookup. The bottleneck is the fusion topology and the loss, not the chemistry features. R1 was therefore confounded (it varied the encoder while holding two suspect factors fixed), so the encoder verdict was recorded as provisional.
meaning: This result set the strategic direction for the whole R-regime. The encoder is not the lever under the MSE + T5-A setup, so the project (i) carried multihot_425 forward as the held-constant chemistry encoder for subsequent tiers (it was both the best arm here and the T-regime lock), (ii) deferred rather than killed the fingerprint question for an R1-revisit after a better architecture and loss were found, and (iii) crucially, promoted chem-kNN (NDCG@5 0.485 / Spearman 0.240) to be the standing promotion-gate baseline for R2, R-LOSS, and all later R-tiers. The decisive read — that a deep model under pointwise MSE cannot beat a gene-specific similarity lookup — redirected effort toward fusion topology and ranking loss as the real candidate levers, and foreshadowed the eventual understanding of the "chem-kNN beats global learning" wall as a memorization regime rather than a fixable modeling gap.

analysis: Both a tiny bilinear model and a large nonlinear one plateau at the same place (~0.43 NDCG@5) and both lose to a simple local lookup (chem-kNN, 0.485). The synthesis pins the mechanism: the useful conditional-essentiality signal is gene-idiosyncratic and LOCAL — it lives in each gene's OWN deviations from the population/bulk condition profile (which itself carries ~0 within-gene signal, per chem-NULL). Any GLOBAL parametric model, regardless of size, minimizes average error over ~54k genes and therefore averages those per-gene idiosyncratic deviations away — they look like cross-gene noise to a shared parameter set. So the linear-MF (13k params, bilinear) and the deep model (2.5M params, nonlinear) converge to the same ceiling: the limiting factor is not the model's expressive power but the global-vs-local structure of the task. 'Capacity buys nothing' means: once you have enough parameters to capture the bulk pattern, adding ~190x more parameters and nonlinearity does not recover the gene-specific signal, because that signal is not learnable by any global function — it must be retrieved from each gene's own history (what kNN does). The linear-MF arm carries a second, sharper meaning (synthesis section 5): its free per-gene latent U[g] is a fitness-AWARE representation learned from scratch on the fitness data, discarding ProteomeLM entirely. That it still ties the frozen-embedding deep model and still loses to kNN shows the warm-task bottleneck is NOT the embedding's fitness-blindness — it is the global-vs-local structure. Even a perfect fitness-aware gene vector, used globally, loses to local lookup.
name: Capacity / nonlinearity (linear-MF vs deep)
hypothesis: Is model CAPACITY (parameter count / nonlinearity) the lever that lets a learned global model beat the chem-kNN lookup baseline on the within-organism warm ranking task? Prediction under test: a high-capacity nonlinear deep network should extract more of the gene-by-condition signal than a tiny bilinear model, and possibly close the gap to the chem-kNN gate. The experiment pits a ~13k-parameter bilinear matrix-factorization model against a ~2.5M-parameter nonlinear deep model on identical eligible validation genes.
how_tested:
Data and task: the within-organism WARM ranking task (R-regime, condition-holdout split). For each gene, the goal is to rank that gene's conditions from most- to least-stressful ("find the top stressors for this gene"). Data are Tn-seq fitness measurements across 23 replicate organisms (the replicate-org subset used for headline numbers: ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya). Scoring is restricted to "eligible val genes" only (genes passing the R-LOCK-1 eligibility filter), and — by the project's denominator-parity rule — the model and every baseline are scored on the IDENTICAL eligible val gene set. The full model population is ~54k genes.

Split: this is condition-holdout, so held-out conditions are 100% disjoint from train (cold columns) — i.e. inductive cold-start matrix completion with chemistry as column-features. Vocab/scalers/eligibility thresholds are fit on train rows only (train-only preprocessing). Runs use 3 model seeds and are aggregated as the mean over eligible val genes (not per-org-balanced).

The two arms compared (the capacity contrast):
1. linear-MF: a bilinear matrix-factorization model, ~13k parameters, whose per-gene representation is a FREE learned latent vector U[g] (a fitness-aware gene embedding learned from scratch on the fitness data, discarding the frozen ProteomeLM embedding).
2. deep model: the "intended" R1 architecture (AdapterResidualMLP), ~2.5M parameters, nonlinear, using the frozen ProteomeLM sequence embedding + media-chemistry features.

Metrics: primary is NDCG@5 (top-5 ranking agreement, k=5); secondary is within-gene Spearman (full-list ordinal agreement). Per the R-LOCK-4 metric contract, metrics are the mean over eligible val genes with a bootstrap CI (n=1000, over genes; hierarchical org->gene bootstrap in later reporting).

Baselines / reference lines on the SAME eligible val genes: (a) chem-kNN — the gate — a local, non-parametric lookup that reads each gene's OWN observed history and interpolates by chemistry similarity (NDCG@5 0.485 / 0.4852); (b) chem-NULL — the population condition profile, gene-identity-free, predicting the same vector for every gene (NDCG@5 ~0.31, Spearman ~0.02); (c) noise floor / ceiling — biological-replicate agreement (NDCG@5 ~0.66 / Spearman ~0.39). Promotion over the gate requires ΔNDCG@5 >= ~0.026 with disjoint hierarchical-bootstrap CIs.

What was actually run and read out: the two capacity arms were trained and evaluated under this harness; their NDCG@5 (and Spearman) were compared head-to-head and against the chem-kNN gate. The finding: the ~13k-param bilinear linear-MF (NDCG@5 0.43, Spearman 0.14) essentially equals the ~2.5M-param nonlinear deep model (NDCG@5 0.42, Spearman 0.13); both plateau at NDCG@5 ~0.42-0.44 and both lose to chem-kNN at 0.485. This sits alongside the parallel encoder sweep (R1) and objective sweep (R-LOSS), all three of which independently returned negative ("all three say no").

results.label: linear-MF (~13k params, bilinear) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures top-5 ranking agreement, ranges 0 (random) to 1 (perfect), higher is better. This tiny ~13k-parameter bilinear model scores 0.43. That is BELOW the chem-kNN lookup gate of 0.485 and well below the replicate ceiling of 0.66 — so it does not beat the simple baseline. The point is that despite being ~190x smaller than the deep model, it matches the deep model's score, showing capacity is not what is limiting performance.

results.label: deep model (~2.5M params, nonlinear) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Same NDCG@5 scale (0-1, higher better). The large ~2.5M-parameter nonlinear deep network scores 0.42 — statistically the same as the tiny bilinear model's 0.43, and again below the chem-kNN gate (0.485) and the ceiling (0.66). Adding ~190x more parameters plus nonlinearity buys essentially nothing: the two land at the same place. Both are net negatives against the gate.

results.label: chem-kNN gate NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: This is the baseline both capacity arms must beat. chem-kNN is a LOCAL, non-parametric lookup that reads each gene's own past measurements and interpolates by chemistry similarity. At 0.485 it outranks both learned global models (0.42 and 0.43). Beating it needs ΔNDCG@5 >= ~0.026 with disjoint CIs — neither arm comes close, so both fail to promote. This is the 'a simple local baseline wins' result.

results.label: linear-MF Spearman (secondary)
results.plain_explanation: Within-gene Spearman is the secondary full-list ranking metric, ranging -1 to 1, higher better; the replicate ceiling is ~0.39 and chem-kNN reaches 0.24. linear-MF's 0.14 is far below both, and only marginally above the deep model's 0.13 — confirming on the secondary metric too that the extra capacity of the deep model adds nothing and both trail the lookup.

results.label: deep model Spearman (secondary)
results.plain_explanation: Same Spearman scale (-1 to 1, ceiling ~0.39, chem-kNN 0.24). The deep model's 0.13 essentially ties the bilinear model's 0.14. Both are far under the local lookup (0.24) and the ceiling (0.39). Reinforces that neither model size nor nonlinearity recovers the gene-specific ordering signal.

results.label: chem-NULL (population profile) NDCG@5 / Spearman
results.plain_explanation: chem-NULL predicts the population's average condition profile for every gene (no gene specificity). Its within-gene Spearman of ~0.02 is essentially zero — meaning the population/cross-gene pattern carries almost NO within-gene signal. This is the mechanistic anchor for 'capacity buys nothing': since the shared/bulk pattern is worthless for ranking, all useful signal lives in each gene's OWN deviations, which a global model of any size averages away.

results.label: replicate ceiling (noise floor) NDCG@5 / Spearman
results.plain_explanation: The best achievable score, set by how well biological replicates of the same experiment agree with each other. NDCG@5 ~0.66 and Spearman ~0.39 — a MODEST ceiling, meaning the target is intrinsically noisy. Context: even the winning chem-kNN (0.485) leaves a real gap to 0.66, and the ~0.42-0.43 models leave more. Shows the plateau is not just 'models are bad' — the whole task has a low ceiling — but the models still sit below the local baseline within that ceiling.

meaning: This is the third independent leg (with encoder/R1 and objective/R-LOSS) of the project's central negative: on the within-organism warm ranking task, a learned GLOBAL model does not beat a simple local chemistry-similarity lookup — and here the specific lever ruled out is model capacity/nonlinearity. 'Capacity buys nothing' is not a tuning complaint; it is structural evidence that the bottleneck is the global-vs-local nature of the task, not model expressiveness. This directly de-risks and de-prioritizes scaling up the network. It also carries the project's sharpest strategic implication (synthesis section 5): because linear-MF's free latent U[g] is itself a fitness-AWARE representation learned from the fitness data, and it still ties the frozen-embedding deep model and still loses to kNN, the warm-task bottleneck is NOT the embedding's fitness-blindness. That is the main argument the project uses to DEFER the expensive fitness-aware-embedding (R-EMB) moonshot for the warm task — a global representation, however good, gets compressed away by global averaging. Together with R1, R-LOSS, and R-HYBRID-A/B, this supports the adopted 'characterization' scope: publish the rigorous, pre-registered negative that the task is memorization-dominated with chem-kNN as a strong baseline learned global models cannot surpass. Note the boundary: this conclusion is warm-only; the later cold-gene diagnostic (R-COLD) showed the global model DOES beat the applicable gate where a gene's own history is removed.
caveats: The capacity arm's exact numbers are reported at ~2-decimal precision in the Scientific Synthesis (linear-MF 0.43 / deep 0.42; Spearman 0.14 / 0.13) rather than as a committed metrics artifact with per-seed CIs, so verification is 'ledger'. The synthesis does not give a separate promotion-gate decision doc for the capacity arm specifically (unlike R1-DEC-001 and R-LOSS-DEC-001, which have their own ledgers); capacity is documented as a bullet within Synthesis section 4 and elaborated in section 5. The R-LOCK-4 decision I read defines the evaluation contract (metrics, baselines, bootstrap, promotion deltas) under which the comparison was scored but is not itself the capacity experiment record. The parameter counts (~13k, ~2.5M) and the 'both ~0.43' framing are quoted directly from the synthesis; I did not independently re-run or re-count parameters. The headline warm numbers used project-wide (model NDCG@5 0.4319, chem-kNN 0.4852) come from the 23-org/3-seed anchor in progress.md; the section-3/4 table rounds these to 0.42 and 0.485.

analysis: The result reveals a locality bottleneck, not an objective bottleneck. Motivated by R1 (encoder didn't matter and a linear matrix-factorization tied the deep model), the team suspected that using a pointwise regression loss (MSE) to optimize a ranking metric was the real limiter. R-LOSS tested that by swapping in dedicated ranking losses — including LambdaRank and ApproxNDCG, which optimize NDCG directly. The finding: none of them helped. Every global parametric model — MSE, Huber, all four ranking losses, and the linear-MF from R1 — clusters at NDCG@5 ~0.40-0.44, a plateau well below the chem-kNN gate (0.485). The one within-family improvement (Huber > MSE, +0.012 NDCG@5) comes from robustness to outlier fitness values, not from ranking-awareness. LambdaRank's NDCG@5 (0.431, 2nd best) with a collapsed Spearman (0.080) is diagnostic: a purely top-focused objective can raise top-of-list agreement slightly while wrecking full-list order, but it still cannot cross the gate. Mechanistically, chem-kNN wins because it exploits each gene's measured behavior at chemically-near conditions locally; a single global weight matrix cannot reproduce that per-gene locality regardless of encoder, objective, or capacity. Two independent levers (encoder in R1, objective here) plus capacity (R1's linear-MF ≈ deep) have all failed, which is what redirects the project toward local/hybrid methods.
caveats: Single split seed only (R-LOCK-2 seed 0); the 3 model seeds vary initialization, not the train/val partition — so these numbers speak to init-robustness, not split-robustness. The per-loss table reports means with sd only for Spearman and NDCG@5 (NDCG@1 and prec@5 are point estimates). The baseline rows (chem-kNN, linear-MF, chem-NULL, noise-floor) are listed without sd. The referenced artifacts (artifacts/runs/rloss/rloss_results.csv, rloss_metric_comparison.csv) are NOT present in the working tree and NOT git-tracked, and the decision file's code_sha is unfilled (`<fill on commit>`), so the numbers are documented only in the ledger, not reproduced from a committed artifact. LambdaRank's Spearman collapse is attributed to the early-stop-on-NDCG@5 criterion; a Spearman+NDCG composite stop was not run and, per the decision, would not close the ~0.05 gate gap anyway. The promotion rule text differs slightly between the two source files: the decision file states delta_spearman >= 0.023 while its prose narrative mentions 0.021 as Huber's actual Spearman gain over MSE (the 0.023 is the threshold, not an achieved value).
how_tested: DATA AND TASK: The within-organism top-k ranking task — for each gene, rank that gene's conditions to surface its top stressors, scored primarily by NDCG@5 (agreement on the top of the ranked list). Inputs are frozen ProteomeLM gene embeddings plus media-chemistry features; the target is Tn-seq fitness. SPLIT: A single fixed data split (R-LOCK-2 split seed 0) was used throughout; every model and baseline was scored on the identical common eligible validation gene set (denominator parity — a hard project rule). SCOPE: 23 replicate organisms (ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya). WHAT WAS VARIED: exactly one thing — the training loss. Six losses were compared: two pointwise (pointwise_mse, the R1 control; and pointwise_huber, a robustness control), two pairwise (pairwise_ranknet; lambdarank, which is NDCG-weighted pairwise and targets NDCG directly), and two listwise (listmle, a listwise permutation loss; approxndcg, a smooth NDCG surrogate that also targets NDCG directly). HELD CONSTANT: the encoder (multihot_425) and the architecture (T5-A, i.e. the AdapterResidualMLP), both pinned from R1-DEC-001, so any difference is attributable to the objective alone. BATCHING (a required methodological detail): pointwise losses were trained ROW-batched (their natural/best form, matching the R1 control), while pairwise and listwise losses were trained GENE-batched (required so a full per-gene list is present to compute pairwise/listwise terms). SEEDS/EPOCHS: each loss was run with 3 model seeds (0,1,2) for 15 epochs; reported per-loss numbers are mean +/- sd over the 3 seeds. BASELINES on the same eligible val genes: chem-kNN (the non-parametric local chemistry-k-nearest-neighbor gate to beat, NDCG@5 0.485), linear-MF (a linear matrix-factorization capacity reference from R1), chem-NULL (a chemistry-only null lower bound), and noise-floor (a replicate-agreement ceiling). PROMOTION RULE (pre-registered): a loss had to beat the chem-kNN gate on NDCG@5 AND achieve a Spearman gain of at least 0.023, with BH-FDR multiple-testing correction across the losses. The primary metrics were NDCG@5 and within-gene Spearman.
hypothesis: H-R-LOSS-01: that the training OBJECTIVE is the bottleneck — that swapping pointwise MSE regression for a ranking loss (pairwise RankNet/LambdaRank or listwise ListMLE/ApproxNDCG, including losses that optimize NDCG directly) would close the gap to the chem-kNN gate (NDCG@5 0.485). The motivation came from R1: since the encoder didn't matter and a linear matrix-factorization matched the deep model, the objective (using MSE to hit a ranking metric) was the suspected lever. The prediction: a ranking loss should beat pointwise MSE and approach or exceed the gate; if it doesn't, the bottleneck lies elsewhere (the local-vs-global nature of the signal).
meaning: This is the second of two independent levers to fail, and it redirects the whole project. Combined with R1 (encoder doesn't matter; linear-MF ≈ deep model on capacity), R-LOSS shows the objective is also not the lever: every global parametric model — regardless of encoder, objective, or capacity — plateaus at NDCG@5 ≈ 0.42-0.44, while a local non-parametric chem-kNN sits at 0.485. The converged conclusion is that the bottleneck is the LOCAL-vs-GLOBAL nature of the signal: kNN exploits each gene's behavior at chemically-near conditions directly, and a single global mapping cannot reproduce that. Concrete consequences recorded in the decision: (1) do NOT pursue fancier NDCG surrogates like NeuralNDCG/differentiable-sorting — LambdaRank already optimizes NDCG directly and lost, so the ~0.05 gap is about locality, not the loss surrogate; (2) DEMOTE R2 (fusion topology), since it is another capacity lever and thus low expected value; (3) PIVOT to a local/hybrid approach (explicit parametric+chem-kNN residual, retrieval/attention over chemically-near train conditions, or local refinement) — proposed as the next tier R-HYBRID; (4) carry pointwise_huber + multihot forward as the parametric base. The one durable positive: Huber is adopted as the default pointwise loss over MSE.
name: Loss family (R-LOSS)

results.label: pointwise_huber NDCG@5 (best loss)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures agreement on the top of each gene's ranked condition list; it runs 0-1, higher is better. Huber was the single best of all six losses, yet 0.435 is still about 0.05 BELOW the chem-kNN gate (0.485) that a learned model must beat, and far below the replicate ceiling (0.66). So even the winning loss fails the promotion gate. The ± .003 over 3 seeds shows this is stable, not noise.

results.label: pointwise_mse NDCG@5 (control)
results.plain_explanation: The R1 baseline objective. At 0.422 it also sits below the 0.485 gate. Huber beats it by +0.012 NDCG@5 — a small but seed-consistent gain from robustness to fitness outliers, not from being ranking-aware. This is the only within-family improvement the experiment found.

results.label: pointwise_huber vs MSE Spearman gain
results.plain_explanation: Within-gene Spearman is the secondary metric — full-list rank agreement (0-1-ish, higher is better). Huber lifts it by +0.021 over MSE, consistent across seeds, reinforcing that robust pointwise regression is the better pointwise choice. But +0.021 is below the pre-registered 0.023 Spearman threshold and, more importantly, neither model beats the gate on the primary NDCG@5 metric.

results.label: lambdarank NDCG@5 and Spearman (the collapse)
results.plain_explanation: LambdaRank optimizes NDCG directly and reached the 2nd-best NDCG@5 (0.431) — still under the 0.485 gate — but its full-list Spearman COLLAPSED to 0.080, roughly half of Huber's 0.151 and well below even MSE's 0.130. This is the headline pathology: a purely top-focused objective can nudge top-of-list agreement while destroying overall list order, so it is not a usable trade. Attributed to early-stopping on NDCG@5 letting it overfit the top.

results.label: pairwise_ranknet NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The simplest ranking loss. At 0.420 it is essentially tied with MSE (0.422) and below both Huber and the gate. Evidence that switching to a pairwise ranking objective does not, by itself, help.

results.label: listmle NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The listwise permutation loss lands at 0.399 — BELOW even the MSE control (0.422). A listwise objective actively hurt here, further undercutting the hypothesis that a ranking loss is the fix.

results.label: approxndcg NDCG@5 (worst loss)
results.plain_explanation: ApproxNDCG, a smooth NDCG surrogate that targets NDCG directly, was the WORST of the six at 0.368 — only modestly above the chem-NULL floor (0.343) and far under the 0.485 gate. Directly optimizing a smooth NDCG proxy did not help and hurt the most, part of why the decision says do not chase fancier NDCG surrogates.

results.label: chem-kNN gate (baseline to beat)
results.plain_explanation: The non-parametric local chemistry-kNN baseline is the gate. No loss beat it — the best learned model (Huber 0.435) is ~0.05 short on NDCG@5, and every model's Spearman (best 0.151) is far under kNN's 0.240. This is the core negative result: local kNN dominates all global parametric objectives.

results.label: linear-MF NDCG@5 (capacity reference)
results.plain_explanation: The R1 linear matrix-factorization scores 0.429 — squarely inside the 0.42-0.44 plateau shared by MSE, Huber, and the ranking losses, and below the 0.485 gate. Its presence in the same band shows the plateau is not about capacity or objective; a simple linear model lands where the deep ranking-loss models do.

results.label: noise-floor ceiling / chem-NULL floor
results.plain_explanation: The replicate-agreement ceiling (0.658) is the practical maximum achievable NDCG@5 and the chem-NULL floor (0.343) is the chemistry-only lower bound. All six losses (0.368-0.435) sit in the lower-middle of this band, closer to the floor than the ceiling and beneath the 0.485 gate — quantifying how much headroom remains and how far global parametric models fall short of it.

name: Top-k-truncated losses (R-TOPK)
hypothesis: H-R-TOPK-01: The prior loss-family experiment (R-LOSS) rejected the ranking losses, but its ApproxNDCG/LambdaRank objectives optimized NDCG over the WHOLE ranked list. The prediction here is that, now that training runs through the proper RankingBatch listwise samplers, a loss that truncates the NDCG gain to the TOP-5 — exactly matching the headline metric NDCG@5 — will close the gap to the chem-kNN gate (NDCG@5 0.485). Rationale: NDCG@5 is the promotion metric, so if any objective could win it should be the one that optimizes precisely that quantity. This was framed as the last objective-axis lever before concluding the objective is not the bottleneck.
how_tested: Design: a pre-registered 5-arm x 3-seed comparison run through the shared R-LOSS handler/runner. Data: the project's within-organism ranking task on Tn-seq fitness, over 23 replicate organisms held constant (ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya). Feature set held constant across all arms: multihot_425 media-chemistry features + the T5-A encoder configuration. Training: 15 epochs per arm, seeds [0,1,2], all arms trained through the RankingBatch listwise samplers (the [B,L]+mask substrate) so the listwise losses see proper per-gene condition lists. The 5 arms were: (1) pointwise_huber — the locked/carried-forward baseline (robust pointwise regression); (2) lambdarank — NDCG-weighted pairwise, top-focused; (3) approxndcg — smooth NDCG surrogate over the whole list; (4) lambdarank_top5 — NEW, the LambdaRank ΔNDCG truncated to the top-5; (5) approxndcg_top5 — NEW, an NDCG@5 surrogate with a top-k gate. Scoring: each arm evaluated on the COMMON eligible validation gene set (denominator parity — model and every arm scored on the identical eligible val genes), reporting seed-mean over 3 seeds of NDCG@5 (primary), within-gene Spearman, and precision@5. Baseline / gate: chem-kNN (NDCG@5 0.4852), the promotion gate a learned model must beat. Promotion rule: beat the chem-kNN gate on NDCG@5 without tanking Spearman. During the run a bug was discovered and fixed: approxndcg_top5 initially FROZE in training (val NDCG@5 flat ~0.354, Spearman ~0) because the top-k gate reused the score-softmax temperature (0.5), making the gate too sharp and the gradient vanish; the fix was a separate gate_temp=2.0 in approxndcg_topk (src/ranking/losses/family.py). Only after this fix did every arm train and get evaluated fairly. A unit test (test_topk_truncation_engages_on_long_lists) guards that the top-k variants are finite, differ from their untruncated form, and prefer a stressor-first ordering. Reproduce: python -m src.cli.run_experiment +experiment=R-TOPK_loss (artifacts in artifacts/runs/rloss/, log topk_full.log).

results.label: pointwise_huber (base) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures agreement on the top-5 of the ranked list, ranges 0-1 with higher=better. The best learned arm scores 0.4319, which is 0.0533 BELOW the chem-kNN gate of 0.485 and well under the replicate ceiling of 0.66. This is the strongest of the five arms but still fails to beat the baseline, so the learned objective does not win.

results.label: pointwise_huber (base) Spearman
results.plain_explanation: Within-gene Spearman (secondary, full-list completeness metric) for the base arm; higher=better. At 0.1522 it is the highest Spearman of the learned arms but far below the chem-kNN baseline's 0.2402, again showing the learned model trails the local baseline even on full-list ordering.

results.label: pointwise_huber (base) precision@5
results.plain_explanation: Fraction of the top-5 predicted conditions that are truly top stressors; higher=better. Base arm 0.4014, below chem-kNN's 0.446, consistent with the NDCG@5 shortfall.

results.label: lambdarank NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Untruncated NDCG-weighted pairwise loss. 0.4289 is slightly below the base arm and 0.0563 under the gate (0.485; higher=better, 0-1 scale) — a ranking loss does not beat robust pointwise regression here.

results.label: lambdarank_top5 (NEW) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The top-5-truncated version of LambdaRank. Critically it scores 0.4239, BELOW its own untruncated counterpart lambdarank (0.4289). Truncating the gradient to the top-5 slightly HURT rather than helped, and it sits 0.0613 under the gate — the central negative result of the experiment.

results.label: approxndcg NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Full-list smooth NDCG surrogate. At 0.3620 it is one of the two worst arms, 0.1232 below the gate, showing the ApproxNDCG family badly underperforms pointwise regression on this task.

results.label: approxndcg_top5 (NEW) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The NDCG@5-surrogate variant (after the gate_temp fix that un-froze training). At 0.3695 it is only marginally above untruncated approxndcg (0.3620) and both are far below the base arm; it is 0.1157 under the gate. So even the loss that most directly targets NDCG@5 fails badly.

results.label: chem-kNN (GATE) NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: The chem-kNN promotion gate — the local baseline a learned model must beat. At 0.4852 (Spearman 0.2402, precision@5 0.446) it exceeds every learned arm, so H-R-TOPK-01 is rejected: no loss, truncated or not, closes the gap to the gate.

results.label: approxndcg_top5 frozen-training symptom (pre-fix)
results.plain_explanation: Before the fix, approxndcg_top5 did not learn at all: val NDCG@5 stuck near 0.354 and Spearman near 0, because the top-k gate reused the score-softmax temperature (0.5), making the gate too sharp and the gradient vanish. The fix (separate gate_temp=2.0 in approxndcg_topk in src/ranking/losses/family.py) un-froze training so the arm could be evaluated fairly — this is why the fixed-run value (0.3695) is meaningful rather than an artifact of a dead optimizer.

analysis: Restricting the loss gradient to the top-5 removes the broader ordering signal without adding any top-end skill that the local chem-kNN baseline does not already possess. Each truncated variant scored below its untruncated counterpart (lambdarank_top5 0.4239 < lambdarank 0.4289; approxndcg_top5 0.3695 only marginally above approxndcg 0.3620 and both far below the base). The best learned objective remains a robust pointwise regression (pointwise_huber, 0.4319), which still trails chem-kNN by 0.0533 on NDCG@5. This is consistent with R-LOSS-DEC-001 and the memorization-dominated finding: the objective is NOT the bottleneck. The remaining gap to chem-kNN is structural — a local-vs-global effect (the local baseline exploits nearby-condition structure the global model cannot) — not a matter of which ranking surrogate is optimized. Separately, the ApproxNDCG training-freeze was a temperature-coupling bug: reusing the sharp score-softmax temperature (0.5) for the top-k gate zeroed the gradient; decoupling it to gate_temp=2.0 restored training and let the arm be judged fairly (it still lost).
meaning: This experiment closes the objective axis for the within-organism warm-ranking task. Having now tested pointwise, pairwise/top-focused, whole-list NDCG surrogate, AND top-5-truncated NDCG-matched losses, none beats the chem-kNN gate, so the project concludes the choice of ranking loss is not what is holding the model back. H-R-TOPK-01 is rejected; pointwise_huber stays the locked objective; the top-k loss variants are retained in the loss registry (tested, cheap to keep) but are NOT promoted. Strategically this redirects effort away from objective engineering and toward the structural local-vs-global gap — the memorization-dominated finding — as the real bottleneck.
caveats: All numbers are seed-mean over 3 seeds (seeds 0,1,2) and are read from the R-TOPK-DEC-001 decision ledger table; they are NOT independently reproduced from a committed metrics artifact in this record (verification=ledger). The 0.485 gate appears as 0.4852 in the arm table and is referred to as ~0.485 in the config header. The approxndcg_top5 value (0.3695) is post-fix; before the gate_temp=2.0 fix the arm was frozen (val NDCG@5 ~0.354, Spearman ~0) and would not have been a fair comparison. No hierarchical-bootstrap CIs are reported in the ledger for these arms; the reject decision rests on point estimates all falling below the gate. Note a wording nuance in the ledger: the truncated ApproxNDCG variant (0.3695) is marginally ABOVE its untruncated form (0.3620), whereas the truncated LambdaRank variant (0.4239) is below its untruncated form (0.4289); the general 'truncation did not help / slightly hurt' claim holds cleanly for LambdaRank and for both families relative to the pointwise base.

name: Static model+kNN ensemble (R-HYBRID-A)
hypothesis: H-R-HYBRID-01: the global parametric model (the frozen-embedding + chemistry MLP) carries signal that is COMPLEMENTARY to the local chem-kNN lookup, so combining the two should beat chem-kNN alone. This is the first test of whether the learned model adds ANYTHING on top of the local lookup — because no standalone global model (from R1 or R-LOSS) had ever beaten chem-kNN by itself. The answer decides whether the project has a genuine model contribution (path: keep hybridizing) or is purely memorization (path: characterization paper).
how_tested: Data and split: The within-organism warm ranking task on the 23 replicate organisms (the headline subset with a reliable replicate noise floor), evaluated on 53,189 eligible validation genes. The task is "rank a gene's conditions to find its top stressors." Two predictors were fused: (1) the standalone global model — a Huber-loss, row-batched MLP over frozen ProteomeLM gene embeddings plus multihot media-chemistry features, which was the R-LOSS loss-family winner; and (2) chem-kNN, the local lookup baseline that is the project's promotion gate. Fusion method: a per-gene z-scored convex combination — for each gene, both the kNN scores and the model scores are z-scored (standardized) within that gene, then blended as alpha*z(kNN) + (1-alpha)*z(model). alpha was swept over [0,1], where alpha=1 is pure kNN and alpha=0 is pure model. First, the full-val alpha-curve was computed over all 53,189 eligible val genes (alpha in {0.0, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0}), which located the curve peak at alpha≈0.8. Because reading the peak off the same val set it is scored on would leak (curve-peeking), an HONEST held-out alpha-selection was then done: the val GENES were split 50/50 by hash into a tune half and a test half; alpha* was chosen to maximize NDCG@5 on the tune half only, then that fixed alpha* (=0.8) was applied and reported on the held-out test half — so the reported hybrid number is out-of-sample, not curve-peeked. Baselines/comparators: the hybrid was compared against pure chem-kNN (the gate) on the identical eligible val genes; a knn+linear-MF convex combo was also run as a reference fusion to check whether the deep model's complement exceeds linear matrix-factorization's. Primary metric NDCG@5 (top-of-list ranking agreement), with within-gene Spearman reported as the secondary full-list metric. Promotion requires clearing the pre-registered delta of roughly +0.023 to +0.026 NDCG@5 over the gate.

results.label: Honest held-out hybrid NDCG@5 (alpha*=0.8 selected on tune-half, reported on test-half)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 runs 0 to 1, higher is better; the chem-kNN gate sits at ~0.485 and the replicate ceiling is ~0.66. The blended model+kNN scores 0.494 versus pure kNN's 0.486 on the same held-out test genes, a +0.008 gain. This is a genuine, out-of-sample (not curve-peeked) win — the model does add complementary signal — but +0.008 is well below the ~0.023-0.026 promotion delta, so it is a real-but-tiny effect: directionally positive, not a promotion.

results.label: Full-val alpha-curve NDCG@5 at the peak (alpha=0.8) vs pure kNN (alpha=1.0)
results.plain_explanation: On the full 53,189-gene val set, the blend peaks at alpha≈0.8 (mostly kNN plus about 20% model), NOT at pure kNN. That the optimum is a mix rather than alpha=1 is the core positive: the learned model contributes signal the local lookup misses. The peak (0.493) sits just above the kNN gate (0.485), again a ~+0.008 gain — good enough to confirm complementarity, not good enough to clear the gate.

results.label: Full-val alpha-curve NDCG@5 at pure model (alpha=0.0)
results.plain_explanation: With alpha=0, the ensemble is the standalone Huber model alone, scoring 0.432 NDCG@5 — clearly below the chem-kNN gate (~0.485). This restates the standing negative: the global model by itself loses to the local lookup. Its value only appears when blended in as a minority (~20%) partner.

results.label: Full-val Spearman at the peak (alpha=0.8) vs pure kNN (alpha=1.0)
results.plain_explanation: Spearman is the secondary, full-list rank-agreement metric (also 0-1-like, higher=better; here on the order of 0.24). The blend improves Spearman from the pure-kNN 0.240 to 0.248 (+0.008) at the same alpha=0.8 peak, so the complementary signal shows up on the completeness metric too, in the same direction and magnitude as NDCG@5 — reinforcing that the gain is real, just small.

results.label: knn+linear-MF reference fusion
results.number: also beats kNN, but by less than knn+model
results.plain_explanation: A convex blend of kNN with linear matrix-factorization also beats pure kNN, but by a smaller margin than the deep-model blend. This is a positive control: it shows the DEEP model's complement is larger than linear-MF's, i.e. the gain is attributable to nonlinear structure the model captures, not merely to any second signal source.

analysis: The peak of the honest alpha-curve landing at alpha≈0.8 (a kNN-dominant mix) rather than at pure kNN is the mechanistic finding: the global parametric model captures cross-gene / sparse-neighborhood structure that the local chem-kNN lookup misses, so a small (~20%) admixture of the model raises top-of-list ranking. The effect is genuine — it holds out-of-sample under a hash-split tune/test alpha-selection (no curve-peeking) and appears on both NDCG@5 and Spearman — but it is tiny (+0.008), far under the ~0.023-0.026 promotion delta. The authors read this as a LOWER BOUND: a crude per-gene z-score convex ensemble is the weakest possible fusion, so +0.008 is the floor of what hybridization can extract, not the ceiling. The knn+linear-MF comparison shows the deep model's complement exceeds linear-MF's, attributing the gain to nonlinear learned structure.
meaning: This is the first positive signal in the warm-split regime that the learned global model is not useless — it captures structure the local lookup cannot, confirming hypothesis H-R-HYBRID-01 directionally. But because the +0.008 gain falls below the locked promotion bar, it is NOT a promotion: the static ensemble does not deliver a model contribution the project can headline. The decision routes to R-HYBRID-B — a learned hybrid (kNN-residual model, retrieval-augmented model, or learned per-example gating alpha(g,c)) expected to extract more of the complementary signal than the crude static blend. The stated go/no-go: if R-HYBRID-B clears the promotion delta, the project has a real model contribution; if it also stalls near +0.01, the complementary signal is genuinely small and the honest scope is the characterization result. (Per progress.md, R-HYBRID-B subsequently also failed to beat the gate, and the warm objective is now understood as memorization-capped.)
caveats: Status of the decision record is "proposed" (not finalized). The reported hybrid gain of +0.008 NDCG@5 is directional and out-of-sample but BELOW the pre-registered promotion delta (~0.023-0.026), so it is explicitly NOT a promotion vs the chem-kNN gate. The full-val alpha-curve numbers (peak 0.493) are curve-peeked and shown only to locate the peak; only the tune/test hash-split number (0.494 vs 0.486) is the honest, leakage-free comparison. No hierarchical-bootstrap CI is reported for this hybrid delta in the source, so CI-disjointness is not established — the +0.008 is a point-estimate win only. The +0.008 is characterized as a LOWER BOUND from the weakest possible (crude z-score) fusion. Reproducibility artifact (rhybrid_alpha_curve.csv) and code path are cited in the ledger but I did not independently open/rerun them, so verification is marked 'ledger' rather than 'code'/'artifact'.

analysis: The mechanism behind the ~0 result is that the within-org conditional-essentiality ranking task is memorization-dominated: the chem-kNN gate wins by retrieving a gene's OWN training history (a local lookup), and the standalone parametric model (AdapterResidualMLP) is a weak global prior. Fusing a weak global signal with a strong local lookup cannot exceed the lookup. Each of the three fusions fails for a specific reason: (a) the residual model adds a continuous model correction on top of knn_loo that helps NDCG@5 marginally (+0.0002) but hurts Spearman (-0.0049), and its per-seed sign-flip (+0.0048/-0.0076/+0.0033) proves the effect is within split-noise, not a stable gain; (b) retrieval-augmentation and (c) learned gating both blend in too much of the weak global prior and REGRESS on both metrics. The learned gate is the clearest diagnostic: it settled at mean_alpha ~0.46 (trusting kNN and model roughly equally in the z-scored blend), but because the model half is weak, any weight moved onto it hurts — the data says 'trust the lookup.' Three orthogonal fusions all converging on ~0 is strong evidence the ceiling is a real property of the task, not a fusion-design artifact. Notably, the learned hybrids extracted LESS complementary signal than R-HYBRID-A's crude static z-score ensemble (+0.008 honest NDCG@5), whose gain came from a fixed, conservative alpha~0.8 (mostly kNN). The Keio single-org dev run gave the residual hybrid a misleadingly large honest +0.042 NDCG@5, but this is a single-org-ceiling artifact (Keio is an easy organism) that vanished under the governing full 23-org multi-org eval, where residual collapsed to ~0.
how_tested:
DATA & SPLIT: The warm within-organism ranking task on the project's canonical Tn-seq fitness data, restricted to the 23 replicate organisms that have a reliable replicate noise floor (the headline eval subset; eligibility_policy.yaml r_replicate_org). Genes are split transductively; evaluation is on the eligible val gene set with the eligibility filter r_lock_1_v1. Sample size: ~52,900-53,200 common eligible val genes shared across models (denominator parity). Run with 3 model seeds (0/1/2), 8 training epochs, k=5 neighbors, weighted-Huber loss, multihot_425 chemistry featurization, and n_bootstrap=1000 for CIs.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN: Three separate LEARNED fusions of the standalone parametric model (AdapterResidualMLP — the T5-A locked model, trained row-batched with weighted-Huber, the R-LOSS winner) with the local chem-kNN gate (k=5, cosine similarity on condition multihot; standalone NDCG@5 ~0.485 / Spearman ~0.24 on full val). (a) RESIDUAL MODEL: added an exclude_self flag to chemistry_knn_predict to enable leave-one-out (LOO) kNN on train; trained AdapterResidualMLP to predict the residual r = fit − knn_loo (train rows with NaN knn_loo dropped); val prediction = knn_val + model_residual_val. (b) RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED MODEL: for each (gene g, condition c), retrieved gene g's k=5 nearest TRAIN conditions by chemistry, built retrieval features [neighbor fits, similarities, weighted-mean fit, coverage], concatenated adapter(gene_emb) + chem_c + retrieval_features, and trained end-to-end with Huber to predict fit; train rows use LOO retrieval, val rows retrieve from TRAIN only. (c) LEARNED GATING: alpha(g,c) = sigmoid(MLP(gate_features)) where gate_features = [distance to nearest train condition, neighborhood density, kNN coverage]; final score = alpha*z(knn) + (1−alpha)*z(model) computed per gene via per-gene z-scoring (as in R-HYBRID-A); alpha's MLP trained on TRAIN (LOO kNN) to match per-gene-z-scored true fit.

BASELINE / GATE: The chem-kNN gate itself (k=5, cosine on condition multihot), scored on the IDENTICAL eligible val gene set as each hybrid (denominator parity). This is the standing project gate a learned model must beat by the promotion delta (~0.026 NDCG@5 / ~0.023 Spearman).

METRICS & STATS: within-gene Spearman with a hierarchical org->gene bootstrap (n=1000), NDCG@1/@3/@5, and precision@5. NDCG@5 is the primary metric. Reported both (i) full-val seed-averaged numbers on the same genes as chem-kNN, and (ii) an HONEST held-out check: val genes split 50/50 by hash, hybrid reported on the test half (none of the three hybrids has a val-selected scalar, so test-half eval is the honest number). Also reported per-seed Δ NDCG@5 to test stability. Leakage discipline: all train-side kNN/retrieval is leave-one-out; all val-side neighbors come from TRAIN only. A separate DEV run on Keio single-organism was used during development.

REFERENCE BARS: chem-kNN gate NDCG@5 ~0.485 / Spearman ~0.24; replicate-agreement noise-floor ceiling NDCG@5 ~0.658 / Spearman ~0.39; promotion delta ~0.026 NDCG@5 / ~0.023 Spearman over the gate.
