hypothesis: H-R-HYBRID-01 (round 2): a LEARNED hybrid of the global parametric model (AdapterResidualMLP) plus the local chem-kNN lookup can extract MORE of the complementary signal than R-HYBRID-A's static z-score ensemble (which gained only +0.008 NDCG@5), ideally clearing the promotion delta (~0.026 NDCG@5 / ~0.023 Spearman over the chem-kNN gate). If even a learned hybrid stalls near +0.01 or worse, the complementary signal is genuinely small and the honest scope is characterization, not a promotable model.
meaning: This closes the modeling thread for the within-organism warm ranking task. Two learned-hybrid rounds (A static, B residual/retrieval/gating) plus the full R1 (encoder), capacity, and R-LOSS (objective) sweeps have ALL now failed to beat the simple chem-kNN lookup by a promotable margin. Three orthogonal fusions converging on ~0 is strong evidence the ceiling is a real property of the task, not a fusion-design artifact — so no fourth hybrid variant was pursued. The honest, publishable result is the rigorous negative: a pre-registered benchmark showing the within-org conditional-essentiality ranking task is memorization-dominated, with a chemistry-similarity lookup as the strong baseline that learned global models cannot surpass. The decision was NO PROMOTION and a pivot to the CHARACTERIZATION scope; recommended follow-ups were the cold-gene diagnostic (the one regime where a global model could in principle help — later run as R-COLD, the project's first positive) and folding these results into SCIENTIFIC_SYNTHESIS.
name: Learned hybrids (R-HYBRID-B)

results.label: Residual hybrid — Δ NDCG@5 vs chem-kNN (full val, seed-avg)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures top-5 ranking agreement on a 0-1 scale where higher is better; the chem-kNN gate sits at ~0.485 and the replicate ceiling at ~0.66. This is a statistical TIE — essentially zero improvement — and it is far below the ~0.026 needed to promote. Bad for the hypothesis: the best of the three fusions does not beat the lookup.

results.label: Residual hybrid — Δ Spearman vs chem-kNN (full val, seed-avg)
results.plain_explanation: Spearman is the secondary full-list ranking metric (0-1-like correlation, higher is better; gate ~0.24). Even the best hybrid REGRESSES slightly here. So the one fusion that ties on the primary metric actually gets worse on the secondary one — no genuine gain.

results.label: Residual hybrid — per-seed Δ NDCG@5 (sign-flips)
results.plain_explanation: The sign of the effect flips across the three random seeds — positive, negative, positive. This is the key evidence that the tiny +0.0002 average is within split-noise, not a stable real gain. A promotable improvement would be the same sign every seed and clearly above the gate.

results.label: Retrieval-augmented hybrid — Δ NDCG@5 / Δ Spearman
results.plain_explanation: Both metrics REGRESS below the chem-kNN gate. Feeding retrieval features into an end-to-end model blends in too much of the weak global prior and makes ranking worse, not better. Clearly bad — moving the wrong direction on both primary and secondary metrics.

results.label: Learned gating hybrid — Δ NDCG@5 / Δ Spearman
results.plain_explanation: The worst of the three: both metrics regress the most below the gate. A learnable blend weight that can ever down-weight the kNN loses ground, because the kNN lookup is the strong signal and the model is weak. Bad — the most flexible fusion does the most damage.

results.label: Learned gating — learned mean alpha
results.plain_explanation: Alpha is the weight on the kNN in the per-gene z-scored blend (1.0 = pure kNN, 0.0 = pure model). The gate settled at ~0.46, trusting the kNN and the model roughly equally. Because the model half is weak, this ~equal weighting HURT relative to leaning almost entirely on the lookup — the data effectively says 'trust the lookup.' This is the mechanistic explanation for why gating regressed.

results.label: Residual hybrid — HONEST held-out Δ NDCG@5 (test half of 50/50 split)
results.plain_explanation: The leakage-clean honest number for the best hybrid: essentially zero, confirming no real gain survives an honest held-out test. Far below the ~0.026 promotion bar. This is the governing verdict for the residual fusion.

results.label: Retrieval / gating — HONEST held-out Δ NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Both other fusions REGRESS on the honest held-out test too, consistent with their full-val numbers. Bad — no fusion clears the gate honestly.

results.label: Keio-only dev run — misleading residual honest Δ NDCG@5
results.number: +0.042 (Keio single-org) → collapses to ~0 on full 23-org eval
results.plain_explanation: During development the residual hybrid looked strongly positive (+0.042, which would clear the ~0.026 promotion bar) on the single organism Keio. But this vanished under the full 23-org multi-org eval (residual -> ~0). It is a single-org-ceiling artifact — Keio is a known-easy organism — and the full-val multi-org number is the honest governing result. A cautionary example of a single-org number overstating a gain.

results.label: Reference: R-HYBRID-A static ensemble (prior round, for comparison)
results.plain_explanation: The earlier crude static z-score ensemble gained +0.008 by fixing a conservative weight of ~0.8 on the kNN. The learned hybrids here extracted LESS than this crude baseline (best honest +0.0009). Counterintuitive but telling: giving the fusion freedom to learn hurt, because it moved weight onto the weak model — reinforcing that the lookup is the honest ceiling.

caveats: NO PROMOTION: none of the three learned hybrids clears the promotion delta (~0.026 NDCG@5 / ~0.023 Spearman) on either co-primary metric. The best (residual) is a statistical tie on NDCG@5 (+0.0002, sign-flipping across seeds: +0.0048/−0.0076/+0.0033) and a small regression on Spearman (−0.0049); honest held-out Δ = +0.0009 confirms ~zero. Retrieval and gating regress on both metrics. Verification is LEDGER-level: numbers are recorded in the decision ledger (R-HYBRID-DEC-002) and cite committed artifacts (artifacts/runs/rhybrid_b/full_results.csv + full_run.log) and passing tests (pytest tests/unit green, 156 passed / 1 skipped), but I read the decision document, not the raw artifact CSV, so I mark this ledger rather than code/artifact. The multi-seed CI bounds elsewhere in the project are summary bands (mean of per-seed CIs), not pooled bootstraps; the Δ significance here rests on point estimates + per-seed sign consistency rather than a paired bootstrap on the per-gene Δ. The Keio-only +0.042 dev number is explicitly a single-org-ceiling artifact and must NOT be read as a result. The metrics_primary in the header list Spearman first (R-LOCK-4 v2), but per the 2026-06-24 project-wide change NDCG@5 is the primary metric everywhere — this record leads with NDCG@5 accordingly.

name: Train-organism augmentation (R-AUG)
hypothesis: H-R-AUG-01: because the headline trains the global model on only the 23 replicate organisms (leaving ~25 embedded feba organisms, including some of the largest, out of training entirely), training the shared encoder on ALL 48 embedded organisms — while evaluating on the same locked 23 organisms against the same chem-kNN gate — should NARROW the model-to-gate gap, since more organisms give the encoder more (protein-embedding, chemistry)->fitness examples to generalize from. This is the cleanest, cheapest test of whether the model-to-gate gap is a training-data-VOLUME problem (fixable with more data, including external Tn-seq datasets) or a STRUCTURAL one (no transferable cross-organism signal).
how_tested:
Data and objective: the project predicts conditional gene essentiality and the active metric is within-organism top-k ranking of a gene's conditions ("find the top stressors for this gene"), scored primarily by NDCG@5 (k=5). The experiment asks whether adding more TRAINING organisms narrows the gap between the learned global model and the chem-kNN baseline (the promotion gate). The headline configuration trains AND evaluates the global model on only the 23 replicate organisms (ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya), leaving the other ~25 embedded feba organisms (including some of the largest: Putida, psRCH2, the pseudo* set, WCS417, Phaeo, Pedo557) contributing zero training rows.

Design (a clean controlled A/B): the same locked model architecture (pointwise_huber loss + multihot_425 chemistry features + T5-A encoder/adapter) was trained TWICE on the IDENTICAL locked evaluation. Arm 1 (base_23org): model trained on the 23 eval organisms only. Arm 2 (aug_48org): model trained on all 48 embedded organisms — the 23 eval organisms plus the 25 extra organisms (config extra_orgs=auto = all embedded organisms minus eval_orgs). Both arms were scored on the identical eligible validation gene set against the identical chem-kNN gate. Settings: 3 model seeds [0,1,2], split_seed=0, 8 epochs.

What was held fixed (the key control): the validation set, R-LOCK-1 gene eligibility, and ALL baselines (chem-kNN gate, chem-NULL, linear-MF) were produced exactly as prepare_r1_data over the 23 eval organisms. The extra 25 organisms contribute ENTIRELY to training and never touch the evaluation. This was implemented via R1Data.baseline_train (baselines score on the locked eval-organism train set) plus prepare_r_aug_data (grafts the extra-organism rows onto the .train split only, and extends the embedding/multihot matrices to the 48-organism union). Crucially, the chem-kNN gate was asserted bit-identical between the two arms (drift = 0.000000), which proves the evaluation is held fixed and only the model's training data changed. This is the one lever that can help ONLY the global model, because chem-kNN is per-organism-local and gains nothing from extra training organisms.

Baselines compared: the chem-kNN gate (primary promotion gate), plus chem-NULL and linear-MF, all scored on the same eligible val genes as the model. Primary metrics: NDCG@5 and within-gene Spearman (prec@5 also reported). Pre-registered promotion rule: augmentation must IMPROVE the model toward the gate (delta-NDCG@5 > 0 vs base, consistent across seeds) to justify ingesting more (including external) organisms. Reproduce command: python -m src.cli.run_experiment +experiment=R-AUG_train_org_augmentation (artifacts in artifacts/runs/raug/).

results.label: aug_48org NDCG@5 (seed-mean, 3 seeds)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 ranges 0 to 1 (higher is better); it measures top-of-list ranking agreement, i.e. how well the model surfaces a gene's true top stressors. This is the model trained on all 48 organisms. At 0.4166 it sits BELOW the chem-kNN gate (0.4852) and well below the replicate ceiling (~0.66), so it does not beat the baseline it must beat. Worse, it is lower than the same model trained on only 23 organisms (0.4319), so adding organisms actively hurt.

results.label: base_23org NDCG@5 (seed-mean, 3 seeds)
results.plain_explanation: The reference arm: the same locked model trained on only the 23 eval organisms. At 0.4319 it is still below the chem-kNN gate (0.4852) and the ~0.66 ceiling (the learned model does not beat chem-kNN even at baseline), but it is the BETTER of the two arms, showing the 23-org training set is preferable to the 48-org one.

results.label: Delta NDCG@5 (aug - base)
results.plain_explanation: The change from adding 25 training organisms is NEGATIVE 0.0152 NDCG@5. The pre-registered rule required a POSITIVE delta to support augmentation; instead the gap to the gate WIDENED. This is the headline negative-transfer result: more training organisms degrade top-of-list ranking on the target organisms.

results.label: Per-seed NDCG@5 (base vs aug, disjoint)
results.plain_explanation: Every single aug seed (max 0.4193) is below every single base seed (min 0.4302); the two groups do not overlap at all. This means the harm from augmentation is a robust, real effect, not seed-to-seed noise, so the conclusion does not hinge on averaging.

results.label: aug_48org within-gene Spearman (seed-mean)
results.plain_explanation: Spearman is the secondary, full-list rank-completeness metric (higher is better). The 48-org model scored 0.1270, down from the 23-org model's 0.1522 (a drop of 0.0252) and far below chem-kNN's 0.2402. So augmentation hurts full-list ranking too, not just the top-5.

results.label: base_23org within-gene Spearman (seed-mean)
results.plain_explanation: The 23-org model's secondary full-list metric. At 0.1522 it beats the augmented arm (0.1270) but is still well under the chem-kNN gate's Spearman of 0.2402, reaffirming that the learned model trails the local baseline on the warm split regardless of training-organism count.

results.label: aug_48org prec@5 (seed-mean)
results.plain_explanation: Precision@5 (higher is better) = fraction of the top-5 predicted conditions that are truly top stressors. The 48-org model hits 0.3870, below the 23-org model's 0.4014 and below chem-kNN's 0.446, the same negative-transfer direction on a third metric.

results.label: base_23org prec@5 (seed-mean)
results.plain_explanation: The 23-org model's precision@5. Higher than the augmented arm (0.3870) but still under chem-kNN (0.446), consistent with the model trailing the local baseline on the warm split.

results.label: chem-kNN gate NDCG@5 (both arms, drift)
results.plain_explanation: chem-kNN is the promotion gate a learned model must beat (~0.485). It reads 0.4852 in BOTH arms with drift exactly 0.000000, because it is per-organism-local and cannot benefit from extra training organisms. The bit-identical gate is the control that proves this is a clean A/B: only the model's training data changed, so the -0.0152 model drop is attributable solely to augmentation, not to any shift in the evaluation.

analysis: The mechanism is negative transfer. The shared encoder weights, when forced to also fit 25 additional heterogeneous organisms whose conditional (protein-embedding, chemistry)->fitness structure does not transfer to the target organisms (the T-regime already measured cross-organism transfer as approximately random), are pulled away from the 23 eval organisms' specific structure. The extra training data is the wrong kind: distribution shift / noise relative to the target organisms rather than reinforcing signal. Because chem-kNN is a per-organism-local baseline, it gains nothing from extra training organisms, so its gate number stays bit-identical (drift 0.000000), making the two arms a clean controlled A/B where ONLY the model's training data changed. Doubling the training organisms (roughly doubling the rows) widened the model-to-gate gap rather than closing it, proving the bottleneck is structural (absence of transferable cross-organism signal), not training-data volume. This is consistent with, and reinforced by, R1 (encoder/capacity don't matter) and R-LOSS/R-TOPK (objective doesn't matter).
meaning: The hypothesis was rejected — and then some, because the sign came out negative. For the within-organism warm-gene headline objective, augmenting training with additional organisms is strictly counterproductive, so the locked configuration keeps the 23-organism training set. Scientifically this closes the training-DATA axis: the model-to-gate gap is structural (absence of transferable cross-organism signal), not a matter of training-data volume. Combined with R-LOSS/R-TOPK (the objective doesn't matter) and R1 (the encoder/capacity don't matter), no global-model lever tried has moved the warm headline — it is memorization-dominated and local. It also empirically backs the 2026-06-18 external-Tn-seq survey's "skip" verdict: adding even MORE DISTANT organisms (MtbTnDB, A. baumannii — different clades and assay methods) would almost certainly worsen negative transfer, so the external-data integration cost is not justified for this objective. The one place a global model could still win — the cold-gene regime, where kNN has no within-organism history to retrieve — is explicitly left open and is the designated next experiment.
caveats: Scope is strictly the warm-gene, within-organism headline metric (chem-kNN's home turf). R-AUG does NOT close the cold-gene regime (genes with no within-organism history for kNN to retrieve); more-diverse training organisms could even HELP there while hurting the warm headline, and the cold-gene diagnostic (materialize_cold_gene) is the designated next experiment. The result is from 3 model seeds at split seed 0, 8 epochs, on the locked 23-organism replicate subset only. Numbers are read from the decision ledger (R-AUG-DEC-001.md) and progress log; the source states artifacts exist at artifacts/runs/raug/ but the figures were verified against the committed ledger, not by re-running or opening the artifact CSVs. Minor source note: the evidence table lists chem-kNN NDCG@5 as 0.4852 while CLAUDE.md's durable gate figure is quoted as ~0.485 (the same number, rounded).

analysis: The experiment tests a reviewer's most obvious objection to the project's central negative result (no global/hybrid deep model beats a local chem-kNN baseline): "your labels are just noisy, so the metric is measuring noise, not model quality." If that were true, denoising the evaluation (keeping only well-measured genes/cells) should let the model catch up to or pass kNN, and/or up-weighting confident labels during training should help. Neither happens. chem-kNN wins in all 4 confidence quartiles and at all 3 cell-level |t| thresholds, and confidence-weighted training slightly hurts (Delta about -0.004). What confidence DOES change is the achievable ceiling: the biological-replicate noise floor rises from 0.586 (Q1) to 0.835 (Q4), and the model-vs-kNN gap narrows from 0.055 to 0.040 (stratified) / 0.050 to 0.010 (cell-filtered) but never reaches zero. Mechanistically this is consistent with the whole R-series: the deficit is local-vs-global, not a fitting or noise problem. A single global model cannot reproduce each gene's idiosyncratic local condition-ranking history, whereas kNN copies it directly from chemically-similar neighbors. Label noise explains PART of the model-to-ceiling gap (the ceiling itself is only 0.59 in Q1, so the low-confidence task is intrinsically noisy) but noise does NOT explain the model-to-kNN gap, which persists at every confidence level. A logged selection-bias caveat: the cell-filter's large apparent NDCG@5 gains come from discarding 39k genes down to 3.3k and isolating big-effect conditions, not from the model getting better; a Keio-only dev signal where the model edged ahead at |t|>=4 did not survive the multi-org run.
caveats: The cell-level high-|t| filter (finding 2) is selection-biased and is reported as a companion, not a headline: raising the threshold discards genes (39,356 -> 8,427 -> 3,276) and isolates big-effect conditions, so nearly all of the rising NDCG@5 comes from an easier surviving problem, not from the model improving. A Keio-only development run had the model edge ahead of kNN at |t|>=4, but this did NOT survive the 23-org multi-org run (another single-organism-ceiling artifact). This is a CHARACTERIZATION decision, not a promotion gate; chem-kNN is used as a reference only. Ceiling values are the biological-replicate noise floor restricted to each stratum's genes. Stratum sizes are approximate (~9.8k genes/stratum, quartiles of the eligible val gene set).
how_tested: DATA AND SPLIT: The locked base ranking model (AdapterResidualMLP + weighted Huber loss + multihot_425 chemistry encoder) was trained and evaluated on the 23 replicate-organism headline subset (ANA3, BFirm, Btheta, Burk376, Caulo, Cola, Cup4G11, Dda3937, Ddia6719, DdiaME23, Dino, DvH, Dyella79, HerbieS, Kang, Keio, Korea, Koxy, MR1, Marino, Methanococcus_JJ, Methanococcus_S2, Miya). Three model seeds (0, 1, 2) were run and results were seed-averaged; training ran 8 epochs. All scoring uses the eligible val gene set with strict denominator parity: the model and every baseline are scored on the identical set of eligible validation genes. The confidence signal is abs_t, the Wetmore-et-al-2015 moderated t-statistic already present in the canonical fitness table (the field-standard |t|>4 = "real effect" threshold); it is carried through the pipeline via prepare_r1_data. THREE PROCEDURES WERE RUN. (1) CONFIDENCE-STRATIFIED EVAL (the primary analysis): eligible val GENES were binned into 4 quartiles (n_strata=4) by their median per-cell abs_t, from Q1 (lowest confidence, median |t|=0.52) to Q4 (highest, median |t|=2.06), roughly 9.8k genes per stratum. Within each stratum, four quantities were computed on the same genes: the deep model, the chem-kNN baseline (k=5), the chem-NULL baseline, each scored by within-gene Spearman AND NDCG@5, plus the biological-replicate noise-floor CEILING restricted to that stratum's genes. (2) CELL-LEVEL HIGH-|t| FILTER (a companion analysis): instead of binning whole genes, each gene's ranked list of conditions was restricted to cells with abs_t >= a threshold of {0, 2, 4}; NDCG@5 was recomputed for model vs kNN on the genes that still had >=5 surviving cells (n_genes: 39,356 at >=0; 8,427 at >=2; 3,276 at >=4). This is explicitly flagged as selection-biased because well-measured cells tend to be big-effect cells, so it is a companion not a headline. (3) t-WEIGHTED TRAINING (a secondary lever): the base model was retrained with each training row's loss weight multiplied by a saturating ramp f(abs_t) that rises to 1 at |t|=4 (|t| capped at 4.0), i.e. loss weight = w_g * f(abs_t); this was compared head-to-head against the w_g-only base, across all 3 seeds. Reproducibility: code in src/experiments/rconf/_rconf_common.py and src/experiments/rconf/run.py; 6 unit tests in tests/unit/test_rconf.py, full suite 161 passed; artifacts written to artifacts/runs/rconf/{stratified.csv, cell_filter.csv, tweight_overall.csv, full_run.log}.
hypothesis: H-R-CONF-01: measurement label NOISE (not model/data structure) explains the deep model's deficit relative to the chem-kNN gate. If true, then (a) on well-measured (high-confidence) rows the model should catch up to kNN, and/or (b) confidence-weighting the training labels should help. The confidence signal is abs_t (Wetmore-2015 moderated t). This directly tests whether the project's central negative result (no global model beats local chem-kNN) is a label-noise artifact or is structural.
meaning: This is a defensive characterization result that hardens the project's central negative rather than overturning it. It pre-empts the single most likely reviewer objection ("your labels are just noisy, so the model is fine and the metric is the problem") with direct data: the model-vs-kNN ranking does NOT flip at any measurement-confidence level, so the deep model's deficit is structural (local-vs-global memorization), not a noise artifact. It simultaneously and honestly quantifies noise: measurement confidence sets a real, confidence-dependent ceiling (only 0.586 achievable at the noisy low end, rising to 0.835 at the clean end), and noise accounts for PART but never all of the gap. Confidence-weighted training being a non-lever (Delta about -0.004) reinforces that the bottleneck is not what a global model fits but that a single global model cannot reproduce each gene's idiosyncratic local history. Practically, the stratified figure/table becomes a characterization-paper exhibit ("performance vs measurement confidence; the negative is noise-robust"), and the finding was folded into SCIENTIFIC_SYNTHESIS. The only remaining regime where a global model could still help (unseen/cold genes) was flagged as the next optional diagnostic.
name: Confidence stratification (R-CONF)

results.label: Q1 (low confidence) gap kNN-model, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: In the lowest-confidence quartile of val genes, chem-kNN's NDCG@5 (0.414) beats the deep model's (0.359) by 0.055. NDCG@5 runs 0-1, higher=better; higher means the top-5 ranked stress conditions for a gene are more right. kNN is ahead, which is bad for the model. Note every method is far below the chem-kNN reference gate of 0.485 here, and even the best-possible score (the biological-replicate ceiling) is only 0.586 - so this low-confidence slice is intrinsically noisy and hard for everyone.

results.label: Q2 gap kNN-model, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Second quartile: kNN (0.431) still beats the model (0.375) by 0.056, essentially the same gap as Q1. The model has not started to catch up as confidence rises slightly. Still bad for the model; both remain below the 0.485 gate and the 0.562 ceiling for this slice.

results.label: Q3 gap kNN-model, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Third quartile: kNN (0.473) beats the model (0.423) by 0.050 - the gap is starting to narrow slightly. Everything is rising with confidence (the ceiling is now 0.626), but the model still loses to kNN, which is the whole point: denoising is not flipping the winner.

results.label: Q4 (high confidence) gap kNN-model, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Highest-confidence quartile: kNN (0.633) still beats the model (0.593) by 0.040 - the narrowest gap, but it never closes. This is the strongest test of the noise hypothesis (cleanest genes, median |t| about 2) and the model STILL loses. Absolute scores are high here (well above the 0.485 gate) only because the ceiling itself rose to 0.835, i.e. the task is easier on well-measured genes - not because the model overtook kNN.

results.label: Ceiling rise across strata (Q1->Q4)
results.plain_explanation: The biological-replicate noise-floor ceiling (the best NDCG@5 any method could hope to reach, given how noisy the measurements are in that slice) climbs from about 0.59 to 0.83 as confidence rises. This quantifies that a large share of the model-to-ceiling gap at the low end is irreducible biological noise: on noisy genes even a perfect model is capped near 0.59. Good context, not a model win.

results.label: Q4 Spearman cross-check
results.plain_explanation: Using the secondary metric (within-gene Spearman, full-list rank agreement, also 0-1-ish higher=better) on the highest-confidence quartile, kNN (0.345) again beats the model (0.300). This confirms the NDCG@5 story is not a top-5-only quirk - the same ordering holds on the completeness metric.

results.label: Cell-filter |t|>=0 (all cells), NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Companion cell-level analysis at the no-filter baseline: across all 39,356 genes the model scores 0.435 vs kNN 0.485 (the project's headline gate value), a 0.050 gap. This is the unfiltered starting point - the model loses by the familiar full-project margin.

results.label: Cell-filter |t|>=2, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: Restricting each gene to cells with |t|>=2 shrinks the set to 8,427 genes and the gap to 0.021. Both scores jump (0.768/0.789) but that jump is a selection artifact - keeping only big-effect cells makes the ranking task easier for everyone. kNN still leads, so denoising at the cell level does not rescue the model.

results.label: Cell-filter |t|>=4, NDCG@5
results.plain_explanation: At the strictest cell filter (|t|>=4, the field-standard real-effect threshold) only 3,276 genes survive and the gap narrows to 0.010 - the smallest of all, but still positive in kNN's favor. The high absolute scores come almost entirely from discarding ~90% of genes and isolating clean big-effect conditions, NOT from the model improving. The gap never reaches zero, so the negative holds even on the cleanest cells.

results.label: t-weighted training effect, Delta(conf - base)
results.plain_explanation: Retraining with confidence-weighted loss (up-weighting high-|t| rows) changed NDCG@5 by -0.0036 and Spearman by -0.0051 versus the unweighted base - i.e. it slightly HURT, consistently across all three seeds. This is bad for the noise hypothesis: if noise were the bottleneck, weighting confident labels should have helped. It did not, so confidence-weighting is not a usable lever.

name: Cold-gene diagnostic — first positive (R-COLD)
hypothesis: H-R-COLD-01: On the project's primary (warm) split, chem-kNN wins only because it retrieves each gene's OWN train history — pure within-gene memorization that is unbeatable and tells us nothing about whether the frozen ProteomeLM embedding carries inductive value. The cold_gene split holds out WHOLE genes (zero train rows), removing memorization by construction. The question: does the frozen embedding carry gene-specific conditional-response signal that GENERALIZES to genes never seen in training, such that a global model beats the only baseline still applicable there (chem-NULL, the gene-identity-free population condition profile)?
how_tested: Data and task: within-organism conditional-essentiality ranking (Tn-seq fitness data), predicting a gene's ordering over its stress conditions. Inputs are frozen ProteomeLM (layer-8) gene embeddings plus media-chemistry features. The single arm tested is the project's locked model configuration: pointwise_huber loss + multihot_425 chemistry features + the T5-A (AdapterResidualMLP) architecture. The key manipulation is the SPLIT: instead of the primary transductive-over-genes split (where each validation gene also has its own train rows), this used the cold_gene split via materialize_cold_gene with held-out fraction 0.20, so whole genes are held out per organism, cold genes have ZERO train rows, and never appear in training. The model early-stops on within-gene Spearman over the held-out cold val genes — no leakage is possible. Baselines and applicability under cold_gene: chem-kNN predicts from a gene's OWN train conditions, which a cold gene lacks, so 0% coverage and structurally inapplicable; linear-MF needs a learned per-gene latent that cannot exist for an unseen gene, so inapplicable and skipped (compute_mf=False); chem-NULL fits a train-gene-MEAN at the chemically-nearest train condition and is gene-identity-free, so it applies and becomes the gate. Denominator parity restricted to {model, chem-NULL} via R1Data.parity_pred_cols, both scored on the IDENTICAL eligible cold val gene set; chem-kNN/linear-MF coverage reported explicitly. Full headline: 23 replicate organisms, 3 model seeds (0,1,2), split seed 0, 8 epochs, n=11,761 eligible cold val genes. Fast confirmation on Keio+Caulo+MR1 (seed 0, n=1,912). Statistics: per-seed comparison (3 seeds) for directional robustness plus a hierarchical (organism→gene) bootstrap 95% CI for BOTH NDCG@5 (primary) and Spearman (secondary) with a model-vs-gate disjointness flag; multi-seed CI bounds are the mean of per-seed CIs. Diagnostic promotion rule: model must beat chem-NULL consistently (ΔNDCG@5 > 0, per-seed disjoint). Regression check: primary-split R-EVAL fast gate reproduced bit-exactly (model 0.4468 / chem-kNN 0.5091) and 125 unit tests passed, confirming the new cold-gene path did not disturb existing behavior. Reproduce fast: python -m src.cli.run_experiment +experiment=R-COLD_cold_gene; full: add experiment.tag=full experiment.model_seeds=[0,1,2] and the 23 replicate orgs. Artifacts in artifacts/runs/rcold/.

results.label: Model NDCG@5 (primary, 23-org / 3-seed, n=11,761)
results.plain_explanation: NDCG@5 measures top-of-list ranking agreement, ranges 0-1, higher is better; it is the project's primary metric. 0.2748 is the model's top-5 accuracy at ranking a cold gene's most-essential conditions. This BEATS the applicable baseline (chem-NULL, 0.2447) and every one of the 3 model seeds sits above the gate, so the win is directionally robust and not seed noise. In absolute terms 0.2748 is modest and far below both the warm-split model (~0.43) and the chem-kNN warm gate (0.485) and the replicate ceiling (0.66) — the cold-gene regime is genuinely harder because there is no own-gene history to lean on.

results.label: chem-NULL NDCG@5 (the gate, 23-org / 3-seed)
results.plain_explanation: chem-NULL is the population condition profile (gene-identity-free), the ONLY baseline applicable to held-out whole genes here, so it is the bar to beat in this regime. 0.2447 is what you get with no gene-specific information at all. The model's 0.2748 exceeds it, meaning the frozen embedding adds real gene-specific signal on genes it never trained on. Note this is a WEAKER bar than the warm-split chem-kNN gate (0.485), so beating it is not a headline promotion.

results.label: ΔNDCG@5 (model − chem-NULL, primary)
results.plain_explanation: A positive gap of +0.0301 NDCG@5 points is the size of the embedding's advantage over the population average on unseen genes. It is consistent (all 3 seeds disjoint above the gate) but small in absolute magnitude — the embedding adds real but modest gene-specificity, not a large effect. For context, the warm-split promotion rule requires ΔNDCG@5 ≳ 0.026 vs the (stronger) chem-kNN gate, so this +0.030 is not comparable to that promotion bar.

results.label: NDCG@5 bootstrap-CI disjointness (primary) — THE KEY NUANCE
results.plain_explanation: This is the central caveat. Although the model's POINT estimate beats chem-NULL on the primary metric across all 3 seeds, the two 95% confidence intervals OVERLAP — so the +0.0301 win is NOT statistically CI-significant on NDCG@5. The reason is that NDCG@5 has higher per-gene variance than Spearman, giving it a wider CI. An earlier record wrongly called the win CI-confirmed on the strength of Spearman alone; that was corrected once NDCG@5 got its own CI (precisely why NDCG@5 is held as the primary metric). Verdict: a strong directional lead to pursue, not a closed/confirmed win.

results.label: Model within-gene Spearman (secondary, 23-org / 3-seed)
results.plain_explanation: Spearman is the secondary, full-list rank-correlation metric (whole-list completeness rather than just the top-5); it also runs -1 to 1, higher is better. 0.0735 is a weak-but-positive correlation between predicted and true condition ordering for cold genes. It beats chem-NULL's 0.0359, and unlike NDCG@5 its 95% CI is DISJOINT from the gate's — so the win IS CI-significant on this secondary metric (though the margin is thin).

results.label: chem-NULL within-gene Spearman (secondary)
results.plain_explanation: The population-baseline full-list rank correlation for cold genes, with no gene-specific information. The model's 0.0735 is about double this and its CI does not overlap [0.0230, 0.0514], establishing a CI-disjoint secondary-metric win. Δ = +0.0376.

results.label: chem-kNN coverage under cold_gene
results.plain_explanation: This 0.0000 is the design-confirming result: chem-kNN, the strong warm-split gate, retrieves a gene's own train conditions, and cold genes have none — so it covers 0% of cold val genes and structurally cannot play. linear-MF is likewise unlearnable for an unseen gene. This is why chem-NULL (not chem-kNN) is the gate here, and it proves the warm-split model→chem-kNN gap is a MEMORIZATION gap (kNN retrieving own-gene offsets), not evidence the embedding carries nothing.

results.label: Fast confirmation (Keio+Caulo+MR1, seed 0, n=1,912)
results.plain_explanation: The small 3-organism confirmation reproduces the same sign and magnitude as the 23-org headline, so the directional win is not an artifact of the full org panel. However, on this smaller set the bootstrap CIs OVERLAP on BOTH metrics (including Spearman), consistent with less statistical power — CI-significance on Spearman needs the full 23-org panel.

analysis: Mechanism: the primary split is transductive over genes, so chem-kNN wins by retrieving each validation gene's own train history — unbeatable within-gene memorization. Holding out WHOLE genes removes that mechanism (chem-kNN coverage collapses to 0.0000, linear-MF becomes unlearnable), leaving chem-NULL (the gene-identity-free population profile) as the only applicable baseline. In that clean setting the global model beats chem-NULL by ΔNDCG@5 +0.0301 and ΔSpearman +0.0376, with point estimates disjoint across all 3 seeds. Therefore the frozen ProteomeLM embedding does carry transferable, gene-specific conditional-response signal that generalizes to unseen genes — the first positive global-model result in the project. The CI nuance is essential and honest: on the PRIMARY metric (NDCG@5) the model and chem-NULL 95% CIs OVERLAP, because NDCG@5's per-gene variance produces a wider CI; only the SECONDARY Spearman is CI-disjoint. So the result is directionally robust (3/3 seeds) and Spearman-CI-disjoint, but does NOT clear a strict disjoint-CI bar on the primary metric. An earlier claim of CI-confirmation rested on Spearman alone and was corrected once NDCG@5 got its own CI.
meaning: This reframes the project's central finding. The warm-split negatives (R1 encoder, R-LOSS/R-TOPK objective, R-HYBRID, R-AUG training-org volume) are a MEMORIZATION-dominance result, not an "embeddings are useless" result: the global model loses to chem-kNN on the warm split only because chem-kNN memorizes each gene's own history, which is unavailable for unseen genes. The cold-gene regime is where the embedding's inductive value is actually visible and where the global model is BEST among applicable methods. Two consequences: (1) it is a diagnostic acceptance of H-R-COLD-01 (directional), NOT a promotion against the locked chem-kNN gate — chem-NULL is a weaker bar than chem-kNN, so no headline number changes; and (2) it opens the one path the warm axes had closed, namely the inductive cold-start-over-genes objective, where more-diverse training organisms (R-AUG's negative transfer was measured warm-only) could plausibly HELP rather than hurt. Recommended firm-up: a paired/pooled bootstrap on the per-gene NDCG@5 Δ (model − chem-NULL), which cancels shared per-gene variance and is more powerful than comparing two marginal CIs, to convert the primary-metric lead into a CI-significant claim.
caveats: This is a DIAGNOSTIC, directional acceptance, not a promotion against the locked R1 gate: the gate here is chem-NULL, a WEAKER bar than the warm-split chem-kNN gate (0.485), so the +0.030 is not comparable to the ΔNDCG@5 ≳ 0.026-vs-chem-kNN promotion rule and no headline number changes. The most important statistical caveat: on the PRIMARY metric (NDCG@5) the model [0.2424, 0.3179] and chem-NULL [0.2118, 0.2823] 95% CIs OVERLAP, so the +0.0301 point-estimate win is NOT CI-significant on the primary metric; only the secondary Spearman is CI-disjoint (0.0735 [0.0523, 0.1034] vs 0.0359 [0.0230, 0.0514], and that margin is thin). The fast 3-org set OVERLAPS on BOTH metrics. Multi-seed CI bounds are the mean of per-seed CIs (a summary band, not a single pooled bootstrap). An earlier record claimed the win was CI-confirmed on Spearman alone; that was corrected once NDCG@5 got its own CI. Recommended firm-up: a paired/pooled bootstrap on the per-gene NDCG@5 Δ (cancels shared per-gene variance). Absolute performance is modest (~0.27, well below the ~0.43 warm split and 0.66 replicate ceiling) — the embedding adds real but small gene-specificity. Numbers are from the decision ledger; no committed metrics artifact was independently re-read for this record.

name: Dark-genome residual miner spike (R-DARK)
hypothesis: Because the project is memorization-capped (chem-kNN beats every learned model at predicting fitness), the proposal flips the question: instead of predicting fitness, treat chem-kNN as a null model of what is chemically predictable and mine its RESIDUAL — the conditional essentiality the lookup cannot explain. The specific hypothesis under test is that unannotated ("dark genome") genes — protein-coding genes with no/hypothetical/DUF/uncharacterized descriptions — are ENRICHED for reproducible, chemically-surprising essentiality (large studentized residuals) relative to annotated genes, so the dark genome is where the surprising conditional biology hides. This is a discovery task, not a ranking task, so NDCG@5 and the chem-kNN promotion gate do NOT apply.
how_tested:
Data: the canonical fitness matrix data/derived/canonical/v0/fitness_experiment_long.parquet (gene x condition fitness `fit`, with `expName`, `gene_key`=orgId:locusId, and a `condition_key` built from media/temperature). Replicates are multiple `expName` rows sharing a `condition_key`. Ran on 3 organisms: Keio, Caulo, MR1. No model training and no GPU — a lightweight residual-mining pass reusing existing loaders and the harness chem-kNN.

Two code versions were built (src/experiments/rdark/spike.py v1, then spike_repro.py v2), both uncommitted. v1 was found flawed: its naive top "surprises" were single-measurement (n_rep=1) artifacts (the low-replication/σ risk that had been predicted), and its gene-permutation null tested predictability rather than surprise-beyond-noise. v2 is the honest test and is the source of the reported numbers.

The v2 procedure per organism: (1) restrict to REPLICATED cells only (n_rep>=2). Keio had 204,606 replicated cells (35,748 orphan/dark), Caulo 284,832 (63,984 orphan), MR1 166,408 (65,296 orphan). (2) Compute chem-kNN expected fitness with chemistry_knn_predict(k=5, exclude_self=True) — exclude_self gives genuine leave-one-condition-out so the expectation never includes the scored cell; the inline kNN was verified against the canonical harness to ~1e-16. (3) Form the studentized residual r* = (observed - expected)/σ(condition). (4) Require the deviation to REPRODUCE across a gene's two replicate halves: both halves |z|>3 vs σ(condition) AND concordant sign; a passing cell is a CONFIRMED surprise. (5) Split cells by annotation via a Gene-table join on (orgId, locusId): dark/orphan = protein-coding (type=1) with desc null/empty or matching hypothetical/DUF/uncharacterized/unknown-function; annotated = the rest.

Two tests were run. GATE (real vs noise): a within-condition replicate-shuffle null — shuffle replicate labels within each condition, recompute residuals, count confirmed surprises surviving by chance; compare the real confirmed-orphan count to the shuffle-null count with an empirical p over 500 permutations (0.0020 is the 500-perm floor). ENRICHMENT (dark MORE surprising than annotated?): compare per-gene confirmed-surprise RATE for orphan vs annotated genes with a label-permutation p (label_p ~1.0 = orphans significantly QUIETER, i.e. the opposite of enriched). The planned Step 4 cross-organism ortholog concordance (Ortholog table, the intended primary non-circular validator) was NOT run — the spike stopped at Steps 1-3 once the enrichment premise failed.

results.label: Keio — confirmed orphan surprises vs shuffle null
results.plain_explanation: In Keio, 794 dark-gene cells passed the reproducible-surprise test, versus only ~76 expected by the replicate-shuffle null — about 10x the noise floor, with emp_p at the 500-permutation floor. This is a GOOD/positive result for the sub-claim that reproducible chemically-unexpected essentiality is real signal, not measurement noise.

results.label: Caulo — confirmed orphan surprises vs shuffle null
results.plain_explanation: In Caulo, 2235 dark-gene surprises vs ~293 from the null — again roughly an order of magnitude above chance at the permutation floor. Confirms the surprise signal is real in a second organism.

results.label: MR1 — confirmed orphan surprises vs shuffle null
results.plain_explanation: In MR1, 2404 dark-gene surprises vs ~234 from the null — ~10x the null, permutation-floor significant. Third organism confirming the residual carries genuine reproducible signal. Across all three orgs the finding 'it is all artifacts' is killed.

results.label: Keio — orphan vs annotated confirmed-surprise RATE
results.plain_explanation: The per-gene surprise rate is LOWER for dark genes (2.2%) than for annotated genes (6.0%); label_p=1.0 means orphans are significantly QUIETER, not richer. This is the key negative: it FALSIFIES the enrichment premise — dark genes are less surprising, the opposite of the hypothesis.

results.label: Caulo — orphan vs annotated confirmed-surprise RATE
results.plain_explanation: Same direction in Caulo: dark 3.5% vs annotated 5.8%, label_p=1.0 (orphans significantly quieter). The enrichment premise fails in a second organism.

results.label: MR1 — orphan vs annotated confirmed-surprise RATE
results.plain_explanation: Same in MR1, and the gap is widest here: dark 3.7% vs annotated 10.2%, label_p=1.0. Across all three orgs the surprising conditional biology is broader and STRONGER in annotated genes — 'the dark genome is special' is dead.

analysis: The mechanism is a clean split of two nested claims. First, the residual DOES carry real biology: after restricting to replicated cells, requiring concordant |z|>3 reproduction across a gene's two replicate halves, and using a proper within-condition replicate-shuffle null, confirmed surprises run ~10x that null in all three organisms (emp_p at the 500-perm floor). So reproducible, chemically-unexpected conditional essentiality is genuine signal, not measurement noise — this kills the 'it's all σ/low-replication artifacts' worry that sank v1. Second, and fatally for the direction, the dark genome is NOT where that signal concentrates: orphan genes have a LOWER confirmed-surprise rate than annotated genes in every org (rate ~0.02–0.04 vs ~0.06–0.10, label_p=1.0 = significantly quieter). The phenomenon is broader and stronger in annotated genes, so the 'unknown genes harbor the surprising biology' hook is unsupported. The deeper problem exposed by the spike: a 'confirmed chemically-unexpected reproducible phenotype' is essentially a specific phenotype, and feba.db's SpecificPhenotype table already catalogs 38,525 of those — so even the real-signal finding has thin novelty over existing annotation.
meaning: This is a fast, cheap (days, no training, no GPU) reframe that reached a clear decision at Step 3 without proceeding to the expensive cross-organism ortholog step. Its verdict: the headline reframe 'the dark genome is special / enriched for surprising essentiality' is DEAD (premise falsified in 3/3 orgs). The one surviving angle is narrow and borderline — the orphan subset of residual-defined (not merely large-|fit|) reproducible surprises, gated on whether Step-4 cross-organism ortholog concordance yields a corroborated subset that existing annotation misses; proceed only if that specific nugget is wanted, and do not headline dark-genome enrichment. For the project as a whole, R-DARK removes the top-ranked reframe candidate (it had been the #1 pick on the reframe slate) from contention, and its falsification was independently re-confirmed by the 2026-06-29 adversarial direction slate (which retracted/demoted 'dark-genome-by-condition' explicitly citing R-DARK). No project code or behavior changed; the R-EVAL regression gate was untouched.

analysis: Mechanism of the finding: The project repeatedly observed that a non-parametric chem-kNN baseline (which predicts a gene's fitness at a held-out condition by looking up THAT SAME gene's fitness at chemically-near conditions) beats every global parametric model — an MLP over frozen ProteomeLM embeddings + chemistry, linear matrix factorization, ranking losses, and capacity scaling. Adding training organisms hurt (negative transfer), and naive score-fusion of model+kNN failed. The natural worry was "this feels like cheating / a data leak." The literature sweep resolves this: chem-kNN winning is the EXPECTED outcome of a named cross-field regime — "local memorization beats global learning." The single most on-point precedent is literally titled for the situation: Khandelwal et al., "Generalization THROUGH Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models" (kNN-LM, ICLR 2020), where a frozen global model is beaten on the long tail by a kNN lookup over its own representation space, and the field's response was to keep the non-parametric memory as a permanent first-class component, not to declare the model a failure. Feldman (STOC 2020) proves long-tail memorization is NECESSARY for near-optimal generalization — if each gene is a rare subpopulation, a smooth global map provably cannot match a memorizer. Grinsztajn (NeurIPS 2022) / McElfresh (NeurIPS 2023) explain that MLPs are too smooth/rotation-invariant for irregular per-instance tabular targets (predicts the capacity-scaling failure). Rendle (RecSys 2020) shows an MLP struggles to even learn a dot product (predicts capacity failure); Dacrema (RecSys 2019) shows simple baselines beat reproducible neural recommenders. Xu/Alon/Neubig (ICML 2023) explain WHY the naive blend fails — the kNN-LM gain comes from representation + distance-temperature, not ensembling — which directly explains R-HYBRID's failure. Ahlmann-Eltze/Huber/Anders (Nature Methods 2025) is the in-domain analog: deep-learning perturbation prediction does not outperform simple linear baselines. So chem-kNN exploits each gene's OWN observed fitness at a chemically-near condition = an in-domain near-neighbor, and a strong in-domain similarity baseline that a model only beats out-of-domain is the textbook expectation, not a leak.
how_tested: This was NOT a code experiment — no model was trained and R-EVAL was untouched (the R-EVAL regression gate stayed bit-exact at model NDCG@5 0.4468 / chem-kNN 0.5091, and no headline number moved). It was a citation-verified multi-agent literature sweep run on 2026-06-25 (the writeup is dated 2026-06-24/25 in the header), spanning 8 research fields. The methodology was a three-stage pipeline per the document header: (1) SEARCH — fan out web searches across the fields; (2) ADVERSARIAL-VERIFY — a verifier agent checked each candidate citation against the actual source text, catching and correcting hallucinated or mis-attributed cites; (3) SYNTHESIZE — map each verified precedent onto the project's specific 'wall.' The precise question put to the literature had two parts: Q1, is 'local memorization beats global learning' a recognized phenomenon or are we cheating/leaking? Q2, what techniques are CATEGORICALLY DIFFERENT from the naive scalar-blend fusion (R-HYBRID) that already failed? The fields swept and the anchor references verified in each: Learning theory (Feldman, STOC 2020, arXiv:1906.05271; Feldman & Zhang, NeurIPS 2020); NLP (Khandelwal kNN-LM, ICLR 2020, arXiv:1911.00172; Xu/Alon/Neubig 'Why do Nearest Neighbor Language Models Work?', ICML 2023); Tabular ML (Grinsztajn, NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2207.08815; McElfresh, NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2305.02997); Recommenders (Cheng Wide&Deep, RecSys 2016, arXiv:1606.07792; Dacrema 'Are We Really Making Much Progress?', RecSys 2019, arXiv:1907.06902; Rendle NCF-vs-MF Revisited, RecSys 2020, arXiv:2005.09683); Cheminformatics/QSAR applicability domain (Sahigara, J. Cheminformatics 2013; Sheridan time-split, JCIM 2013); plus in-domain genomics (Ahlmann-Eltze/Huber/Anders, Nature Methods 2025, PMC12328236). The verifier explicitly flagged the genomics framing as having the weakest citation reliability, so only the Ahlmann-Eltze paper is treated as solidly verified in-domain and is framed as an ANALOG, not the same task. The verification stage produced five documented corrections (recorded in the source): Dacrema is '6 of 7' reproducible neural methods beaten (not the '11 of 12' that circulates); a personal-transcriptome cite conflated two separate Nature Genetics 2023 companion papers (Huang et al. s41588-023-01574-w vs Sasse et al. s41588-023-01524-6); 'one PCA still rules them all' is Bendidi et al. (NeurIPS 2024 wksp), not fabricated names; the activity-cliff 'memorization' framing belongs to Elangovan 2021 / Walters 2024, not van Tilborg 2022; and genomics-specific perturbation benchmarks (PertEval-scFM, Systema, Rastogi/Mostafavi) surfaced as plausible but were NOT text-verified and were flagged as fetch-before-citing. The synthesis then mapped the three observed project failure modes onto predictions from the literature (capacity failure -> Rendle/Grinsztajn; negative transfer from more organisms -> Feldman long-tail dilution; naive fusion failure -> Xu/Alon/Neubig) and concluded chem-kNN winning is EXPECTED. Output artifact: research_log/LITERATURE_local_vs_global_memorization.md, a synthesis document (the 'ledger'), not a committed numeric artifact.
hypothesis: The project's recurring wall — a non-parametric chem-kNN (which retrieves a gene's own fitness at chemically-near conditions) beats every global parametric model, adding organisms hurts, and naive model+kNN fusion fails — was suspected to be either a modeling failure or a data leak ('this feels like cheating'). The hypothesis put to the literature: is 'local memorization beats global learning' a named, characterized phenomenon across fields rather than a bug or leak, such that chem-kNN winning is the EXPECTED in-domain outcome? And, secondarily, which published techniques are categorically different from the failed naive scalar-blend fusion?

results.label: Fields where the regime is named/characterized
results.number: ≥5 fields (learning theory, NLP, tabular ML, recommenders, QSAR/cheminformatics; plus an in-domain genomics analog)
results.plain_explanation: The 'local memorization beats global learning' pattern is not idiosyncratic to this project — it is independently documented as a named, characterized regime in at least five distinct research fields. This is the core verdict: the wall is expected, well-precedented behavior, so chem-kNN winning is NOT a leak or a modeling failure. Good for the project's scientific credibility, because it converts a nagging 'are we cheating?' worry into a citable phenomenon and justifies reframing the project around characterizing the regime rather than fruitlessly trying to beat the local baseline.

results.label: Most on-point precedent (kNN-LM)
results.number: Khandelwal et al., 'Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models,' ICLR 2020, arXiv:1911.00172
results.plain_explanation: The single closest precedent, whose title literally describes the project's situation: a FROZEN global model is beaten on the long tail by a kNN lookup over its own representation space. Crucially, the field's response was NOT 'the model failed' — it was to keep the non-parametric memory as a permanent first-class component. This is the strongest evidence that the project's outcome is the normal, published pattern, and it directly motivates a principled local+global hybrid rather than abandoning the model.

results.label: Learning-theory basis (Feldman)
results.number: Feldman, 'Does Learning Require Memorization? A Short Tale about a Long Tail,' STOC 2020, arXiv:1906.05271 (+ Feldman & Zhang, NeurIPS 2020)
results.plain_explanation: Proves that long-tail memorization is NECESSARY for near-optimal generalization. Applied here: if each gene behaves like a rare subpopulation, a smooth global map provably CANNOT match a memorizer — so the model losing to chem-kNN on warm genes is a theorem, not a tuning bug. It also explains why adding organisms hurt (averaging dilutes the per-gene memorized structure). This is why the project decided NOT to retry augmentation or more capacity.

results.label: Why naive fusion failed (Xu/Alon/Neubig)
results.number: Xu, Alon, Neubig, 'Why do Nearest Neighbor Language Models Work?', ICML 2023
results.plain_explanation: Explains that the kNN-LM gain comes from representation + distance-temperature, NOT from ensembling — which directly explains why the project's naive single-scalar-blend hybrid (R-HYBRID) failed. This is load-bearing: it tells the project the failure was inherent to naive blending, and points to categorically different successors (ResMem residual memorization, Correct-and-Smooth, an adaptive per-query Meta-k gate) rather than re-tuning a blend weight.

meaning: This diligence closes the strategic question of whether the warm 'beat chem-kNN' objective is a fixable modeling gap: it is not — it is a named, cross-field regime, so chem-kNN winning is expected and is not a leak. The consequences for the whole project are concrete and directive: (1) STOP pursuing global-model fixes for the warm ranking task — more MLP capacity/depth, more training organisms / global pooling, and any naive scalar-λ blend are all explicitly ruled out as documented weak versions, and the project's own R-TOPK, R-AUG, R1, and R-HYBRID negatives are now understood as predicted by theory. (2) The realistic ceiling on warm genes is to MATCH a learned-local method (EASE/TabR) or CORRECT its residual (ResMem), never to beat kNN everywhere. (3) The genuine generalization win lives on cold genes / out-of-applicability-domain — validating the R-COLD cold-gene positive as the real signal and reframing the warm negative as a MEMORIZATION gap (kNN retrieves a gene's own history), not an 'embeddings are useless' result. (4) It defines a publishable reframe: a rigorous characterization of a memorization-dominated conditional-essentiality task (strong tuned baseline, denominator parity, hierarchical-bootstrap CIs, similarity-stratified / applicability-domain-aware evaluation, the cold-gene generalization result, and a principled local+global hybrid), where 'this feels like cheating' becomes the thesis. It also produced a concrete, ranked menu of categorically-different next techniques (Tier 1: ResMem, Correct-and-Smooth, adaptive Meta-k gate; Tier 2: EASE, TabR, metric learning) that reuse the locked model + existing chem-kNN datastore and preserve the cold-gene win by construction. Per progress.md, direction remains under the project lead's review (reframe-and-publish vs a different question vs wind down), with an explicit hold on new global-model architectures for the warm task.
